about.accessibilityPresetsText: When a patron is struggling with the interface, staff can help them fix it in seconds. Eight one-click presets designed for the way different minds work:
about.alaStatement: We subscribe to the American Library Association's Library Bill of Rights and the Freedom to Read Statement. These aren't just posters on our wall. They're how we operate. If you have concerns about something in our collection, we genuinely want to hear from you. Start the conversation at the front desk or email us at
about.artificialScarcity: per borrower, artificial scarcity for a file that could be copied infinitely
about.bookRemoval: When Someone Wants a Book Removed
about.bookRemovalIntro: It happens. People feel strongly about what's on our shelves, and we respect that enough to have a real process, not a rubber stamp in either direction.

about.digitalIntro: For years we relied on commercial digital platforms because our patrons needed digital access. But the economics were never fair to libraries, and the model has only gotten worse. We decided it was time to do something about it.
about.doInstead1Suffix: , a free open-source platform built by libraries, for libraries
about.doInstead3: Partnering directly with independent authors and small presses

about.interfaceAdapts: The interface adapts to the patron, not the other way around.
about.languageLiteracyText: Seven languages with full right-to-left support for Arabic. Plain language transformation at a 6th-grade reading level. Device lending programs that bridge the digital divide. Immigrant services from day one.
about.licenseExpiry: or 2 years, then the license expires and we buy it again
about.meetTheStaffSub: A ragtag band of book lovers, technology enthusiasts, and community champions.
about.noCutsStrong: We haven't cut a single position.
about.noCutsText: Staff went from spending 60% of their time on routine queries (password resets, catalog navigation) to 25%. The time they got back went into 40+ new programs, community outreach, and actual research assistance: genealogy, local history, the work that made them want to be librarians.
about.oldModelProblem: The problem with the old model
about.ourPositionText: Every person has the right to choose what they read, and the right not to read something. No one has the right to make that choice for someone else. We curate our collection thoughtfully (that's our job), but we don't remove materials because they make some people uncomfortable. Discomfort and harm are different things.
about.pageSubtitle: Figure it out, make it work, help everyone.
about.pageTitle: The Most Useful Place in Town
about.palace1: Built by LYRASIS, a nonprofit library cooperative
about.palace2: No per-circulation fees, no platform lock-in
about.palace3: Patron data stays with the library, not a vendor
about.palace4: Open source, so we can audit and contribute to the code
about.physicalVsEbook: When you borrow a physical book, we buy it once and lend it until it falls apart. Simple. When you borrow an ebook through commercial platforms, we're renting access under terms set by publishers who charge libraries 3-5x the consumer price. Some publishers won't sell to libraries at all, or they embargo new releases for months. Pay-per-use models look simpler, but costs add up fast and we have no say in the catalog.
about.platformControl: Worse, these platforms control the relationship between our library and our patrons. The reading data, the recommendations, the interface: all of it belongs to a corporation, not to us and not to you. When major platforms changed hands through private equity acquisitions, that made the stakes even clearer. Our patrons' reading habits shouldn't be a line item on a leveraged buyout spreadsheet.
about.poweredByOpenSourceText: L30 is AGPL-3.0 licensed — free to use, modify, and share, with the requirement that improvements stay open. Your data and your future belong to you, permanently. No vendor lock-in, no export fees, no surprises.
about.privacyFirstText: Sessions are wiped when you close the tab. No search logging. No reading profiles. Your data stays on a server in our building, never in the cloud, never for sale.
about.problemText: Our catalog search was broken. Digital resources lived in seven different places with seven different logins. Staff spent more time troubleshooting passwords than doing actual research. Seniors felt left behind. Parents couldn't find books reflecting their families' stories. Something had to change.

about.storyParagraph1: In 1952, a group of book lovers pooled their personal collections and opened in a donated storefront with 500 books. Over seventy years later, we’ve become something they never imagined. You can borrow a laptop, consult a lawyer, fix your bike, learn to weld, get your taxes done, print a resume, record a podcast, and yes, still check out a book. The spirit of that first lending library never went anywhere: figure it out, make it work, help everyone.
about.storyParagraph2: Today we’re the place where people come to figure things out. A place where every brain can find what it needs, where teenagers discover what they’re capable of, and where newcomers start building a life. We’re also still figuring some things out ourselves.
about.testimonial1Text: "I used to be afraid of computers. Now I come in three times a week. She helped me find books about my mother's village in Taiwan, books I didn't even know existed. And she never makes me feel slow."
about.testimonial2Text: "My son asked for books with Black astronauts. The old system gave us nothing. The new recommendation tool gave us six titles, including one by a local author. We've read them all twice."
about.thisIsYourLibrarySub: Stop by with a question, a project, or nothing at all. We’re here.

about.transitionNote: This transition is complete. We're now running entirely on open platforms we control. Our digital collection lives on infrastructure that answers to libraries instead of shareholders.
about.transparentText: Every feature includes plain-language explanations. We publish our AI Evaluation Scorecard so you can hold us accountable.
about.whatWeDidText: We could have bought a vendor solution. We didn't. Big tech's off-the-shelf tools meant cloud storage of patron data, opaque algorithms, and zero community input. So we spent 18 months building our own system on a server in our back closet, guided by listening sessions with seniors, parents, teens, and staff.
about.whatWeWorryAboutText: Is it perfect? No. We worry about over-reliance on tools our small team has to maintain. We worry that future budget pressures could turn "staff have more time" into "we need fewer staff." We worry about the biases we haven't found yet. We publish our scorecard not because we're proud of every number, but because accountability requires sunlight. We'd rather you see where we fall short than trust us blindly.
about.whyBuiltOwnTools: Why We Built Our Own Tools
about.whyIndieAuthorsText: The Big Five publishers set the terms that make digital lending so expensive. Independent authors, on the other hand, are often thrilled to work with libraries directly. We can negotiate fair prices, get files we truly own, and introduce our patrons to voices they won't find on bestseller lists. It's better for authors (who get a real partnership instead of pennies from Amazon), better for patrons (who get a more diverse catalog), and better for our budget. Every submission goes through automated quality checks and staff review before it reaches the catalog, so the collection stays curated without gatekeeping based on viewpoint or genre.

about.directorNoteParagraph1: If you've been here, you already know what this place is. Kids sprawled on the floor with picture books. Regulars saving their favorite chair by the window. Somebody's grandma asking about interlibrary loan for the third time this week (we love her). What started as a shared table and a handful of donated books became this — a place that belongs to you.
about.directorNoteParagraph2: We’re small, and we like it that way. That means we can say yes to the programs our community actually needs, move fast when something isn’t working, and put every dollar toward the people who walk through our doors.

legend.trigger: What do the mood tags mean?
legend.title: Mood tags explained
legend.intro: Mood tags describe how a title feels, so you can pick by what you're in the mood for. Tap any tag to browse more like it.
legend.calm: Quiet, low-stakes, easy to put down and pick back up.
legend.hopeful: Ends in a better place than it starts; leaves you lifted.
legend.intense: High-stakes and gripping. On audiobooks this describes the story's content (tension, violence, distress), not a loud or fast narration.
legend.dark: Heavy themes (grief, dread, the worst of people). Not necessarily sad, but not light.
legend.mindBending: Plays with ideas, reality, or structure; expect to think.
legend.personal: Intimate, first-person, identity-forward. Often memoir or own-voices.

getStarted.subtitle: Three simple steps to start using everything your library has to offer.
getStarted.title: Get Started at the Library

step1.title: Search the Catalog
step1.content:
Ready to find something to read, watch, or listen to?

Before you start, you will need:
• Your library card number
• Your library account password or PIN

Here's how to search:

1. Go to the Catalog page (click "Catalog" in the top menu)
2. Type what you're looking for in the search bar
   - A book title, author name, or topic
   - Example: "mystery novels" or "Michelle Obama"
3. Press Enter or click Search

You'll see a list of matching items with:
• Title and author
• Format (book, DVD, audiobook, etc.)
• Availability at each branch

Use the filters on the left to narrow results by format, branch, or availability.
step1.tip1: You don't need the exact title — partial matches work great
step1.tip2: Use the format filter to find only audiobooks or DVDs
step1.tip3: Sort by "Newest first" to see recently added items
step1.tip4: You can search from the homepage search bar too

step2.title: Find Your Item
step2.content:
Click on any item in the search results to see its detail page.

On the detail page you'll find:
• Full description and details
• Available formats (hardcover, paperback, large print, etc.)
• Which branches have copies
• Current availability status:
  - "Available" — on the shelf now
  - "Checked Out" — someone has it, but you can place a hold
  - "In Transit" — moving between branches
  - "On Hold" — reserved for someone

If the item shows "Available" at your branch, you can go pick it up right now!

If it's checked out or at another branch, placing a hold is the way to go.
step2.tip1: Check multiple formats — the audiobook might be available even if the print book isn't
step2.tip2: The detail page shows how many people are waiting if there's a hold queue
step2.tip3: You can add items to a reading list to save them for later

step3.title: Click "Place Hold"
step3.content:
On the item's detail page, look for the "Place Hold" button. It's usually a prominent orange button.

When you click it:
1. A confirmation dialog will appear
2. It shows the item title and format
3. You may see a format dropdown if multiple formats are available
   - Pick the one you want (hardcover, paperback, large print, etc.)

Note: You need to be logged in to place a hold. If you're not logged in, you'll be asked to sign in first.
step3.tip1: You can place holds from search results too — look for the hold icon
step3.tip2: If you're not logged in, clicking "Place Hold" will prompt you to sign in
step3.tip3: You can hold up to 25 items at a time

step4.title: Choose Your Pickup Branch
step4.content:
After clicking "Place Hold," you'll be asked to select a pickup branch.

The dropdown shows all library branches:
• Your home branch is selected by default (if you set one during registration)
• Each branch shows its name and address
• Pick whichever branch is most convenient for you

The item will be sent to your chosen branch when it becomes available.

You can change your home branch anytime in your account settings.
step4.tip1: Set a home branch in your account so it's always pre-selected
step4.tip2: You can pick up at any branch — it doesn't have to be your home branch
step4.tip3: Items from other branches usually arrive within 1-3 days

step5.title: Confirm Your Hold
step5.content:
Click "Confirm" to finalize your hold.

You'll see:
• A success message: "Hold placed successfully!"
• The item now appears in your "My Holds" list

You'll be notified when the item is ready for pickup:
• Email notification (default)
• Text notification (if you opted in during registration)

Pickup window:
• You'll have 7 days to pick up the item once it's ready
• If you can't make it, the hold will be cancelled and the item goes to the next person in line
step5.tip1: Check your email (including spam folder) for hold notifications
step5.tip2: You can set up text notifications in your account preferences
step5.tip3: If you need more time, call the branch — they may be able to extend your pickup window

step6.title: Track Your Hold
step6.content:
You can check on all your holds from your account:

1. Click your profile icon or go to "Account"
2. Click the "Holds" tab

Your holds list shows:
• Item title and format
• Pickup branch
• Status:
  - "Pending" — waiting for an available copy
  - "In Transit" — a copy is on its way to your branch
  - "Ready for Pickup" — it's waiting for you at the desk!
• Your position in the queue (e.g., "3rd in line")
• Estimated wait time

You can also:
• Cancel a hold you no longer want
• Change the pickup branch
• Pause a hold (useful if you're traveling)

That covers it. You now know how to place and manage holds.
step6.tip1: The "My Holds" link on the homepage is a quick shortcut
step6.tip2: Cancelling a hold frees up your hold slot for another item
step6.tip3: You can pause and resume holds without losing your place in line
step6.tip4: Popular items may have longer wait times — consider alternate formats

careers.whyWorkHereP1: We are not your average library. We are building something new, blending traditional library values with modern technology, inclusive design, and a genuine commitment to community.
careers.whyWorkHereP2: Our team includes librarians, developers, designers, community organizers, and people who do not fit neatly into any category. What we all share is a belief that libraries can be the most transformative institutions in any community.
careers.whyWorkHereP3: We offer competitive salaries, excellent benefits, and a work culture that values curiosity, autonomy, and making a real difference.
careers.thinkingAboutSubtitle: Whether you are a seasoned professional or just starting to explore, here is what you should know.
careers.careerPathsPoint1: Public services, technical services, youth services, digital services, administration
careers.careerPathsPoint2: Emerging roles in AI literacy, data science, UX design, and community development

careers.professionalGrowthPoint2: Internal mentoring, cross-training, and leadership development programs

values.communityFirstDesc: A library card should be the great equalizer. Every service we build, from search to legal aid to home delivery, exists to serve people who need it most.
values.radicalLearningDesc: We do not just help patrons learn. We learn constantly ourselves. Our staff are expected to grow, experiment, and stay curious about new tools and community needs.
values.dignityPrivacyDesc: What a patron reads, researches, or asks for help with is their business. We guard intellectual freedom and data privacy as core professional values.
values.techAsCareDesc: We do not adopt technology to be impressive. We adopt it because it helps a homebound patron get books, a family find legal resources, or a kid discover a love of making.

careers.sampleRolesNote: Sample roles for reference. Live postings will appear above when positions are open.
careers.whyWorkHereBody1: This is a working public library that takes its staff seriously. We pay fair wages, post our pay ranges up front, and protect time for the learning and rest that make this work sustainable.
careers.whyWorkHereBody2: Day to day, our team helps patrons find what they need, runs programs, builds the collection, keeps the technology working, and looks out for the people in our community who get overlooked. We have librarians, technologists, community navigators, makers, and privacy specialists, and we lean on each other.
careers.whyWorkHereBody3: If you believe a library card is one of the most useful things a person can have, and you want to do that work with people who feel the same way, you would fit in here.
careers.valuesIntro: Our team is united by these core principles that guide everything we do.

careers.whatToExpectApplyHeading: What to Expect When You Apply
careers.whatToExpectApplyBody: We try to make hiring clear and low stress. Here is each step, start to finish.
careers.interviewStep1Desc: We read every application. You will hear back from a real person, usually within two weeks, whether or not we move forward.
careers.interviewStep2Desc: A 30 minute conversation with the hiring manager about your experience and the role. No trick questions.
careers.interviewStep3Desc: About 90 minutes with two or three team members. We will share the questions ahead of time so you can prepare.
careers.interviewStep4Desc: We check references, then make an offer that includes the pay range and benefits up front.
careers.newToLibraryWorkBody: Library work is part educator, part technologist, part community advocate. Here is what the pathway looks like.
careers.educationBody: An MLS/MLIS opens doors, but we value demonstrated skill and diverse backgrounds. Library science, social work, IT, education, and community health all prepare you for this work.
careers.careerPathsBody: Modern library roles span community services, technology, data privacy, creative programming, and specialized reference, far beyond the traditional desk.
careers.professionalGrowthBody: The field keeps changing. We invest in continuous learning with certifications, conferences, and dedicated on-the-clock growth time for every staff member.

aITools.plainSummaryBody: These are free tools anyone with a library card can use. They help you find books, write a letter, or ask a quick question. They run on a server in our back room. Nothing you type leaves the building. We do not save your questions, and your session is wiped when you close the tab. Prefer to talk to a person? Call us or come in. Staff is always the first choice.

aITools.dataFlowHeading: Where each tool sends your data
aITools.dataFlowLead: The promise above is in plain language. This is the per-tool receipt. "Leaves our network" means the request travels over the public internet to an AI vendor; "In our building" means it stops at our server.
aITools.dataFlowPatronLead: Everything on the public site runs on the library server. Nothing in this table leaves our network.
aITools.dataFlowStaffLead: Some staff-only tools send data to outside AI providers. We list them here so the picture is complete -- patron content doesn't flow into them.
aITools.dataFlowFootnote: Sourced from the live backend code. If a tool is missing, ask Stevie -- it probably means we haven't built it yet.
aITools.wrongnessLead: We publish what our AI got wrong, what is actually true, and what we changed in response. New entries appear here when we find them.
aITools.wrongnessEmpty: No incidents to report yet. When we find a mistake worth correcting, we will list it here with the date, the tool, what was wrong, and what we changed.

bannedBooks.viewBanTracker: View national data on the Ban Tracker
bannedBooks.nationalBanTrackerDesc: Explore reported book bans and challenges from across the country, with source and coverage details.
bannedBooks.nationalContextAla: The American Library Association documented 4,235 unique titles challenged in 2025. It reports that 92% of challenges were initiated by pressure groups, government officials, or other decision makers, while fewer than 3% originated with individual parents.
bannedBooks.nationalContextPen: PEN America separately recorded 6,870 instances of school book bans affecting nearly 4,000 unique titles during the 2024-25 school year. These totals use different definitions, sources, and reporting periods, so they should not be added together.
bannedBooks.nationalContextEvidence: The pattern is organized as well as local. In a recorded 2024 coalition webinar, a rating-site founder described using BookLooks ratings and compiling district data to help trigger statewide removals. The linked evidence record includes the recording, transcript excerpts, and source grading.
bannedBooks.nationalDataCaveat: National figures are snapshots of reported incidents; many challenges are never reported. Local statistics below describe this library only.
bannedBooks.takeActionDesc: Find your representatives and use letter templates to advocate against book bans.
bannedBooks.talkToLibrarianDesc: Many concerns are resolved with a quick conversation. A librarian can explain how a material was selected and help you find alternatives. Please reach out before filing a formal request.
bannedBooks.librariesAreBastionsOfIntellectual: Libraries are bastions of intellectual freedom. We believe in the right to read, the freedom of thought, and access to diverse perspectives. Here you can learn about our commitment to these values and how we handle challenges to library materials.
bannedBooks.l30CommunityLibraryIsCommitted: {{libraryName}} is committed to providing materials that represent diverse viewpoints on a wide range of topics. We support the freedom to read and oppose censorship. When materials are challenged, we follow a fair and transparent review process guided by the American Library Association's Library Bill of Rights.
bannedBooks.exploreTheBooksOurCommunity: Explore the books our community and others have challenged. Every banned book is a story someone tried to silence — and every checkout is a quiet act of support for the freedom to read.
bannedBooks.browseBannedBooksInOur: Browse Banned Books in Our Catalog
bannedBooks.signUpForBannedBooksWeek: Sign Up for Banned Books Week
bannedBooks.challengeStatisticsWillBeDisplayed: Challenge statistics will be displayed here as data becomes available.
bannedBooks.transparencyIsImportantToUs: Transparency is important to us. Here are some of the challenges our library has faced and how we responded. We share these stories to help our community understand our commitment to intellectual freedom.

faq.a1: MetisLibrary is a new library-led ebook co-op. It offers a shared catalog of indie and open-access content, and grows as more libraries join. Our library is an early member. Every title is reviewed by library staff, and authors are paid directly.
faq.q2: Why did the library switch away from commercial digital platforms?
faq.a2: The costs were unsustainable and the value kept shrinking. Companies kept merging, which meant fewer choices and higher prices. Some services charged us every time a patron checked out a book, making budgets unpredictable. With MetisLibrary, you now have more variety from a library-controlled source with staff-vetted indie authors paid directly.
faq.q3: Most of these services don't have waitlists?
faq.a3: Most content is available instantly. MetisLibrary, Freegal, and Project Gutenberg all offer immediate access on most titles. Some popular indie titles may have a short wait.
faq.q4: Why can't I use Ancestry from home?
faq.a4: Ancestry Library Edition is licensed for in-library use only. This is a publisher restriction, not ours. The home version (Ancestry.com) requires a personal subscription.
faq.q5: Is the library using AI to pick my books?
faq.a5: No. Our collections are curated by real library staff, not algorithms.
faq.a6: MetisLibrary is designed with privacy in mind. Your personal information is scrambled so it cannot be traced back to you, and it is never shared with outside companies. For third-party services like Freegal, we link to each privacy policy so you can decide. Our in-library AI tools run locally and do not send your data anywhere. If you want us to look into a specific service, ask.
faq.q7: Can I still get bestsellers like I could on Libby?
faq.a7: Our digital collection focuses on independent authors and public domain classics. For bestselling titles, we still have print copies on our shelves and can get most books through interlibrary loan (free, usually 1-2 weeks). We know this is a change, and we appreciate your patience as our indie catalog grows.
faq.q8: I have a Kindle. Can I still borrow eBooks?
faq.a8: Kindle does not natively support the EPUB format used by most library apps. Your options: (1) Use the Send to Kindle feature to transfer EPUB files. (2) Project Gutenberg offers Kindle-format downloads for all 77,000+ classics. (3) Use the Palace Project app on your phone or tablet alongside your Kindle. We are happy to walk you through any of these at the reference desk.
faq.q9: What happened to Libby and OverDrive?
faq.a9: We ended our OverDrive subscription in March 2026. We understand many of you relied on Libby and we appreciate your patience with this change. The savings were reinvested in MetisLibrary and expanded maker resources. If you had reading lists or holds in Libby, those are no longer accessible through us. Bring your list to the reference desk and we will help you find those books.
faq.a10: Download the free Palace Project app. It has audiobooks alongside eBooks, all borrowable with your library card. Physical audiobooks on CD are also available at all branches.

gutenberg.faqWhatIsProjectGutenbergA: Project Gutenberg is the oldest digital library, founded in 1971. It offers over 75,000 free eBooks, primarily works that have entered the public domain in the United States. These are books whose copyright has expired, making them freely available to everyone.
gutenberg.faqAreTheseBooksReallyA: Yes, completely free with no strings attached. These books are in the public domain, which means their copyright has expired. You can download them, read them on any device, share them, and even use them for creative projects.
gutenberg.faqWhatFormatsAreAvailableA: Project Gutenberg offers books in multiple formats including EPUB (works with most e-readers), Kindle-compatible formats, HTML (read in your browser), and plain text. This means you can read on virtually any device.
gutenberg.faqDoINeedALibraryQ: Do I need a library card?
gutenberg.faqDoINeedALibraryA: No library card needed. Project Gutenberg is completely separate from our library system - it's a free public resource available to everyone worldwide. We're just helping you discover it.
gutenberg.faqWhatHappenedToOurQ: What happened to our old digital vendors?
gutenberg.faqWhatHappenedToOurA: We canceled our commercial digital platform contracts. The costs were unsustainable and the value kept shrinking, driven by private equity ownership. We reinvested those dollars in Palace Project (free, open-source ebooks), our Indie Authors program, MakerSpace 3.0, and free resources like Project Gutenberg.
gutenberg.faqCanIUseTheseQ: Can I use these for school projects?
gutenberg.faqCanIUseTheseA: Absolutely. Public domain texts are perfect for academic use - you can quote them freely, analyze them, and reference them in papers. Just remember to cite your sources properly.
gutenberg.freeEbooksNoWaitlistsNo: 70,000+ free eBooks. No waitlists. No library card needed. Yours to keep forever.
gutenberg.whyWereCancelingCommercialDigital: Why We're Canceling Commercial Digital Platforms
gutenberg.andWhyProjectGutenbergMatters: And why Project Gutenberg matters more than ever
gutenberg.eachYearWeSpentMore: Each year we spent more and received less value. The costs climbed at a pace we could not sustain. Stressful on staff, stressful on patrons, and the math stopped working.
gutenberg.ourVendorsWereAcquiredBy: Our vendors were acquired by private equity. The pattern is textbook: prices go up, licensing terms get worse, and the platform extracts more value from libraries while delivering less. We refused to keep feeding that cycle.
gutenberg.weWantToBeGood: We want to be good stewards of your tax funds. Every dollar we sent to a private equity firm was a dollar that did not go back into our community.
gutenberg.asASystemABoardAnd: As a system, a board, and a community, we decided to reinvest those dollars in ourselves:

checkPrintJobsGuide.checkStatusInYourLibrary: Check Status in Your Library Account
checkPrintJobsGuide.checkStatusInPersonAt: Check Status In Person at the Library
checkPrintJobsGuide.afterPrintingContent:
Once you've sent the job, here's what to do:

1. Check Your Account Immediately
   • Log into library account right away
   • Confirm your job shows in the system
   • Check the status
   • Better to know right away if something failed

2. Wait Patiently
   • Jobs usually start within 5 minutes
   • Don't think it failed if you don't see it immediately
   • Give it time to queue

3. Pick Up Promptly
   • Once "READY", go get it soon
   • Documents are kept for about 30 days
   • Going right away ensures you get correct job
checkPrintJobsGuide.afterPrintingTip1: Check status right away so you know if something failed
checkPrintJobsGuide.afterPrintingTip2: Documents are kept for about 30 days
checkPrintJobsGuide.beforeYouPrintContent:
A few checks before you hit "Print" can save time and money:

1. Preview Your Document
   • Open the file you want to print
   • Check that it looks right
   • Make sure it's not 500 pages by accident!
   • See how many pages it will be
   • Close if not ready to print

2. Check Your Settings
   Computer Windows:
   • Go to Print (Ctrl+P)
   • Before clicking "Print":
     ✓ Check printer name
     ✓ Check # of pages
     ✓ Check color vs B&W
     ✓ Check paper size
   • Then click "Print"

   Mac:
   • Go to File → Print (Command+P)
   • Before clicking "Print":
     ✓ Check printer name (should be library printer)
     ✓ Check # of pages
     ✓ Check color vs B&W
   • Then click "Print"

3. If Cost Matters
   • Ask staff the price for your number of pages
   • Color printing = more expensive
   • B&W = $0.10/page (usual rate)
   • Calculate before sending

4. Check File Format
   • PDFs print best (most reliable)
   • Word documents (.docx) usually fine
   • Google Docs might print differently than expected
   • Images may come out different sizes
checkPrintJobsGuide.beforeYouPrintTip1: Preview = fewer problems and happier printing
checkPrintJobsGuide.beforeYouPrintTip2: Ask questions BEFORE printing if worried about cost
checkPrintJobsGuide.beforeYouPrintTip3: Staff can help you preview if unsure how
checkPrintJobsGuide.checkAtDeskContent:
If you can't check online, ask library staff:

What to Do:
1. Go to the main circulation desk
2. Tell staff: "I sent a print job. Can you check the status?"
3. Provide:
   • Your library card number, OR
   • Your name and birthdate
4. Staff will look it up in the system
5. They'll tell you:
   • If it's printed and ready
   • If it's still in the queue
   • If there was a problem

What If It's Ready?
1. Staff will fetch your documents
2. They'll show you what was printed
3. They'll tell you the cost (if any)
4. You can pay with cash or card
5. Take your documents and you're done!

What If It's Still Printing?
1. Staff will tell you approximately how long
2. You can:
   • Wait and check back
   • Ask them to hold it
   • Check online later
   • Come back another time (they'll keep it safe)
checkPrintJobsGuide.checkAtDeskTip1: Staff usually have your job found within 2 minutes
checkPrintJobsGuide.checkAtDeskTip2: Bring your library card for fastest service
checkPrintJobsGuide.checkAtDeskTip3: Staff are used to this question - ask anytime.
checkPrintJobsGuide.checkAtDeskTip4: Your documents are kept safely at the desk
checkPrintJobsGuide.checkLibraryAccountContent:
The quickest way to check your print job status:

Step 1: Log Into Your Account
1. Go to the library website
2. Click "Log In" or "My Account"
3. Enter your library card number
4. Enter your password or PIN
5. Click "Sign In"

Step 2: Find Print Jobs
1. Once logged in, look for:
   - "Account" section
   - "My Prints" or "Print Jobs" tab
   - "Documents" or "Files" area
2. You should see a list of your recent print jobs

Step 3: Check Status
Look for one of these statuses:

[QUEUED] Waiting
• Your job is in line to print
• Will start printing soon
• Usually starts within 5 minutes

[PRINTING] In Progress
• Your job is currently printing
• Will be done in a few minutes
• Check back shortly

[READY] Complete
• Your job has finished printing.
• Go to the print station to pick it up
• You may need to pay at the desk

[FAILED] Error
• Your job didn't print
• Reason usually shown (low ink, paper jam, etc.)
• Try printing again from your device

Step 4: Find Your Documents
1. When status shows "READY"
2. Go to the print station in the library
3. Tell staff: "I have a print job ready"
4. They'll get your documents
5. Pay if needed ($0.10/page B&W)
checkPrintJobsGuide.checkLibraryAccountTip1: Check your account first - quickest way to get status
checkPrintJobsGuide.checkLibraryAccountTip2: Print jobs usually start within 5 minutes of sending
checkPrintJobsGuide.checkLibraryAccountTip3: If your job says FAILED, try printing again
checkPrintJobsGuide.checkLibraryAccountTip4: Staff can help locate your documents if unsure
checkPrintJobsGuide.completeContent:
You now know how to check your print status!

Quick Summary:
✓ Log into your account to check status online (fastest)
✓ Ask staff at the desk to look it up (easiest if having trouble)
✓ Status shows: QUEUED, PRINTING, READY, or FAILED
✓ Pick up documents at the circulation desk when ready
✓ If FAILED, just try printing again

For Future Printing:
✓ Preview your document first
✓ Check print settings (B&W vs color, page count)
✓ Know the cost before printing big jobs
✓ Check your account right after printing
✓ Pick up promptly when READY

If You Get Stuck:
• Ask staff - they help with printing all day
• Come back to this guide for troubleshooting
• Staff can reprints from the original file if needed
• Printing problems are fixable.

Questions?
• Visit the print station
• Call the library
• Chat with staff at the desk
• We're here to help!
checkPrintJobsGuide.completeTip1: Staff would rather help than have you wait unsure
checkPrintJobsGuide.completeTip2: Printing is one of the most common help requests - very normal
checkPrintJobsGuide.completeTip3: Come back to this guide anytime you're unsure
checkPrintJobsGuide.introContent:
Need to know if your print job is printing, waiting, or ready to pick up?

Before you start, you will need:
• Your library card number
• Your library account password or PIN
• A device with internet access (to check online)

This guide covers:
✓ Where to check if your job is queued (waiting to print)
✓ How to see if your job is currently printing
✓ Where to pick up your printed documents
✓ What to do if your job didn't print
checkPrintJobsGuide.introTip1: Most print jobs start within a few minutes
checkPrintJobsGuide.introTip2: Jobs are typically printed in order received
checkPrintJobsGuide.introTip3: If you just sent the job, it may still be processing
checkPrintJobsGuide.pageDescription: Find out if your print job is queued, printing, or ready to pick up
checkPrintJobsGuide.problemCostWasHigher: Problem: Cost Was Higher Than Expected
checkPrintJobsGuide.troubleshootingCostContent:
If your print job cost more than you expected:

What happened:
• Color pages cost more than B&W
• Large file used more pages
• Multiple jobs combined onto bill

Solution:
1. Ask staff to itemize the charges
2. They can show what printed
3. Clarify pricing if different than expected
4. For future: preview your document before printing
5. Ask staff about volume discounts if regular user
checkPrintJobsGuide.troubleshootingCostTip1: If unsure about cost, ask staff BEFORE printing
checkPrintJobsGuide.troubleshootingCostTip2: B&W is usually $0.10/page - color costs more
checkPrintJobsGuide.troubleshootingFailedContent:
If your status shows FAILED or your job doesn't appear:

Status Shows "FAILED":
What happened:
• Printer ran out of paper
• Printer ran out of ink
• Paper jam in the printer
• Printer was offline

Solution:
1. Log back into your account
2. Find the failed job
3. Click "Retry" or "Print Again"
4. Job gets sent back to the printer
5. It will print now that problem is fixed

Job Doesn't Appear in Account:
What happened:
• Job may still be processing (takes a minute)
• Job may have gone to wrong printer
• Job sent but account didn't save it

Solution:
1. Wait a few minutes and refresh
2. Try printing again (send it a second time)
3. Go to desk and ask staff to search by:
   • Your name
   • Library card number
   • Time you sent the job
4. Staff can see all recent jobs in the system
checkPrintJobsGuide.troubleshootingFailedTip1: FAILED just means retry - not a big deal
checkPrintJobsGuide.troubleshootingFailedTip2: Printer problems are usually fixed within minutes
checkPrintJobsGuide.troubleshootingFailedTip3: Staff can see all recent jobs in the system
checkPrintJobsGuide.troubleshootingWrongContent:
If your job printed but the documents are missing or wrong:

What happened:
• You picked up wrong job (similar name?)
• Documents already discarded (kept 30 days)
• Print job went to different branch

Solution:
1. Ask staff: "I sent a job on [date/time], but I don't have it"
2. Staff will check their lost & found
3. Describe what the job was (how many pages, what topic)
4. They may find it or be able to reprint
5. If over 30 days old, it has been removed for privacy
checkPrintJobsGuide.troubleshootingWrongTip1: Staff have seen every issue - never embarrassing to ask
checkPrintJobsGuide.troubleshootingWrongTip2: Preview your document before sending 10-page jobs
checkPrintJobsGuide.whilePrintingContent:
What to do at the library computer when you're ready to print:

1. Look at "Print Preview"
   • On Windows: Ctrl+P usually shows preview
   • On Mac: Command+P usually shows preview
   • Make sure it looks right before printing
   • Cancel if it doesn't look correct

2. Send to Correct Printer
   • Make sure you select library printer name
   • Don't send to "Microsoft Print to PDF"
   • Don't send to "Default Printer" unless you're sure

3. Wait for Confirmation
   • After you hit "Print"
   • Look for a message: "Print job sent"
   • Or on library computer: "Document printing"
   • Don't close the dialog right away
   • Wait for the job to process
checkPrintJobsGuide.whilePrintingTip1: Double-check the printer name before clicking Print
checkPrintJobsGuide.whilePrintingTip2: Most printing issues are fixed before you leave

emailAccountGuide.stepFillOutTheSign: Step 3: Fill Out the Sign-Up Form
emailAccountGuide.chooseServiceContent:
There are several free email options available. We recommend:

Gmail (Google):
• Very popular and easy to use
• Excellent spam protection
• Works on all devices
• Visit: gmail.com

Outlook (Microsoft):
• Good alternative to Gmail
• Integrates with Microsoft Office
• Works on all devices
• Visit: outlook.com

Yahoo Mail:
• Another popular option
• Easy recovery options
• Works on all devices
• Visit: mail.yahoo.com

For this guide, we'll use Gmail. You can always create multiple accounts!
emailAccountGuide.chooseServiceTip1: Gmail is widely used and recommended for beginners
emailAccountGuide.chooseServiceTip2: You can switch between services later if you want
emailAccountGuide.chooseServiceTip3: The steps are similar for most email providers
emailAccountGuide.fillFormContent:
The form will ask for these details. Take your time filling it out:

First Name:
• Enter your first name

Last Name:
• Enter your last name

Username (Your Email Address):
• Choose something simple like: john.smith or jsmith123
• Gmail will add "@gmail.com" automatically
• If your choice is taken, Gmail suggests alternatives
• Avoid using special characters or spaces

Password:
• Create a strong password with:
  - At least 8 characters
  - Mix of uppercase and lowercase letters
  - At least one number
  - At least one special character (!@#$%^&*)
• Example: PurpleFrog-Reads-Books42

Confirm Password:
• Type your password again exactly as you entered it
emailAccountGuide.fillFormTip1: Choose a username you'll remember easily
emailAccountGuide.fillFormTip2: Don't include personal information like your birthday or address
emailAccountGuide.fillFormTip3: Write down your password somewhere safe at first (not on a sticky note)
emailAccountGuide.fillFormTip4: Make passwords unique - don't use the same one for other accounts
emailAccountGuide.fillFormTroubleshooting: If your username is taken: Gmail suggests alternatives - choose one that looks good to you. If the password is too weak, add more numbers or special characters.
emailAccountGuide.introContent:
An email account allows you to send and receive messages online. This guide will help you create a free email address using Gmail, which is one of the most popular email services.

Before you start, you will need:
• A device with internet access
• A phone number (for account verification)
• About 10 minutes

By the end of this guide, you'll have:
✓ Your own email address
✓ Knowledge of how to send and receive emails
✓ Ability to use email for library communications
emailAccountGuide.introTip1: Email is completely free with Gmail
emailAccountGuide.introTip2: You can use email on any device with internet
emailAccountGuide.introTip3: Keep your password safe and secret
emailAccountGuide.keepEmailSafeContent:
Now that you have an email account, protect it:

Strong Password Reminder:
• Never use your birth date or name
• Don't share your password with anyone
• Use different passwords for different accounts
• If someone asks for your password, it's a scam

Security Tips:
1. Log out when done, especially on shared computers
2. Never click suspicious links in emails
3. Be careful with attachments from people you don't know
4. Enable 2-Factor Authentication (extra security layer)

Setting Up 2-Factor Authentication:
1. Go to Google Account (myaccount.google.com)
2. Click "Security" on the left
3. Under "How you sign in," enable "2-Step Verification"
4. Follow the prompts to confirm with your phone

This makes your account much safer!
emailAccountGuide.keepEmailSafeTip1: Library staff can help you set up 2-Factor Authentication
emailAccountGuide.keepEmailSafeTip2: It only takes a few extra seconds when you log in
emailAccountGuide.newInboxContent:
Your email account is ready.

You'll see:
• A welcome message from Google
• Your inbox (where incoming emails appear)
• Folders on the left (Starred, Important, Drafts, etc.)
• A compose button to write new emails

Your email address is now:
[your-username]@gmail.com

Take a moment to explore:
1. Click "Compose" to see how to write an email
2. Look at the folders on the left side
3. Check out the settings (gear icon)
emailAccountGuide.newInboxTip1: Your Gmail is accessible from any device
emailAccountGuide.newInboxTip2: You can check email on your computer, phone, or tablet
emailAccountGuide.nextStepsContent:
You now have an email account! Here's what you can do next:

Access Your Email:
• Computer: Gmail.com (bookmark it!)
• Phone: Download the Gmail app from your app store
• Works offline on phones

Using Email for:
• Contacting the library
• Signing up for services online
• Staying in touch with friends and family
• Receiving confirmations and receipts

Getting Help:
• Contact us at the library tech desk
• Ask staff to help with any questions
• Take our "Email Essentials" class (details at tech desk)
• Visit our tech support page for more guides

You're all set! Your new email address is ready to use.
emailAccountGuide.nextStepsTip1: The library offers free email classes for beginners
emailAccountGuide.nextStepsTip2: You can always change your recovery options later
emailAccountGuide.openGmailContent:
Now let's go to Gmail:

1. Open your web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge)
2. In the address bar, type: gmail.com
3. Press Enter on your keyboard
4. You should see the Gmail sign-up page
5. Look for the link that says "Create account" or "Sign up"
6. Click on it

The Gmail sign-up page will appear with a form asking for your information.
emailAccountGuide.openGmailTip1: Make sure you're on the official Gmail website (gmail.com)
emailAccountGuide.openGmailTip2: If you already have a Google account, you can use it
emailAccountGuide.openGmailTip3: The page should look professional with Google's logo at the top
emailAccountGuide.openGmailTroubleshooting: If the page won't load: 1) Check your internet connection, 2) Try a different browser, 3) Clear your browser cache and refresh
emailAccountGuide.pageDescription: Learn how to create your own free email address with Gmail
emailAccountGuide.personalInfoContent:
Next, Gmail asks for more details:

Phone Number (Optional but recommended):
• Enter your phone number for account recovery
• This helps you regain access if you forget your password
• Gmail will send you a verification code via text message
• You'll enter the code to confirm

Recovery Email (Optional):
• You can add another email address you already have
• This also helps with account recovery

Birth Date:
• Choose your birth month, day, and year
• Used for account security and age verification

Gender:
• Select your gender from the options provided

After filling these in, click "Next" or "Continue"
emailAccountGuide.personalInfoTip1: Adding a phone number makes your account more secure
emailAccountGuide.personalInfoTip2: Recovery email is helpful if you forget your password
emailAccountGuide.personalInfoTip3: You're not required to provide all information, but it's recommended
emailAccountGuide.sendFirstEmailContent:
Let's send a test email to make sure everything works:

1. Click the "Compose" button (usually in the top left)
2. A new message window opens

To: [someone's email address]
• Enter an email address of someone you know
• Or you can send it to yourself to test
• Your own email: [your-username]@gmail.com

Subject:
• Type a short title for your email
• Example: "Test Email" or "Hello from my new email!"

Message:
• Click in the body area and type your message
• Say something like: "This is my first email!"

Sending:
1. Look for a "Send" button (usually at the bottom)
2. Click "Send"
3. You'll see a confirmation message

That's it! Your email has been sent.
emailAccountGuide.sendFirstEmailTip1: Always double-check the recipient email address
emailAccountGuide.sendFirstEmailTip2: Emails arrive within seconds (or minutes on slower connections)
emailAccountGuide.sendFirstEmailTip3: You can add attachments (photos, documents) before sending
emailAccountGuide.termsPrivacyContent:
Google will show you their terms of service and privacy policy:

You'll see:
• Google's Terms of Service
• Privacy policy information
• A checkbox to accept the terms

What you need to do:
1. Review the information (it's okay to skip reading the full text at first)
2. Check the box that says "I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy"
3. Click the "Create Account" button

Don't worry - these are standard agreements that every free email service uses. They explain how Google protects your information.
emailAccountGuide.termsPrivacyTip1: You're agreeing to Google's standard terms
emailAccountGuide.termsPrivacyTip2: Your email address and settings are private
emailAccountGuide.termsPrivacyTip3: You can change privacy settings anytime after creating the account
emailAccountGuide.verifyAccountContent:
Google sends a verification code to confirm you're real:

If you provided a phone number:
1. Google will send you a text message with a verification code
2. Enter the code in the field shown
3. Click "Verify"

If you provided a recovery email:
1. Check that email for a message from Google
2. Click the verification link in the email
3. Or enter the code from the email

This step takes just a few minutes. Once verified, you'll have your own email account!
emailAccountGuide.verifyAccountTip1: Check your text messages or email quickly - codes expire in a few minutes
emailAccountGuide.verifyAccountTip2: If you didn't get a code, click "Send code again"
emailAccountGuide.verifyAccountTip3: You might need to check your spam folder for the email
emailAccountGuide.verifyAccountTroubleshooting: If you didn't get a code: 1) Click "Resend code", 2) Check your spam folder, 3) Make sure your phone number or email is correct

emailOnPhoneGuide.checkYourEmailOnYour: Check Your Email on Your Phone
emailOnPhoneGuide.stepGetNotifiedOfNew: Step 4: Get Notified of New Emails
emailOnPhoneGuide.addGmailAndroidContent:
Adding Gmail on Android:

Option A: Using Gmail App
1. Open the Gmail app
2. Tap your profile picture (top right)
3. Tap "Add another account"
4. Select "Google"
5. Type your Gmail address
6. Tap "Next"
7. Type your Gmail password
8. Tap "Next"
9. Follow any security screens
10. Allow permissions
11. Your Gmail is added!

Option B: Using Android Settings
1. Go to "Settings"
2. Find "Accounts" or "Accounts & sync"
3. Tap "Add account"
4. Select "Google"
5. Type your Gmail address
6. Tap "Next"
7. Enter your password
8. Tap "Next"
9. Allow permissions
10. Done!

Note:

emailOnPhoneGuide.addGmailIphoneTip3: Your password is secure - sent directly to Google

emailOnPhoneGuide.addOutlookContent:
For Outlook.com or other email accounts using Outlook app:

iPhone:

emailOnPhoneGuide.beforeStartContent:

emailOnPhoneGuide.downloadAndroidContent:
Android phones can use Gmail, Outlook, or Yahoo Mail apps:

Gmail App (Easiest for Gmail accounts):

Or Download Email Apps:

emailOnPhoneGuide.firstUseContent:

iPhone:

Android:

iPhone Mail:

emailOnPhoneGuide.introContent:
Want to check your email anywhere? This guide shows you how to set up Gmail, Outlook, or Yahoo Mail on your phone.

You'll learn:

emailOnPhoneGuide.introTip2: Works on iPhone, Android, and most devices
emailOnPhoneGuide.introTip3: Takes about 5-10 minutes to set up
emailOnPhoneGuide.multipleAccountsContent:
You can check more than one email account on the same phone:

iPhone:
• You can add multiple accounts
• Mail app shows all of them
• Tap account name to switch

Android:

To add another account, follow the same steps you used to set up your first one.

emailOnPhoneGuide.notificationsContent:
Want your phone to alert you when new emails arrive?

iPhone Mail:
1. Go to Settings → Notifications
2. Scroll down and find "Mail"
3. Tap it
4. Turn on "Allow Notifications"
5. Select notification style (banner, sound, etc.)
6. You'll now see alerts for new emails!

iPhone Gmail:
1. Open Gmail app
2. Tap your profile → Settings
3. Tap your email account
4. Scroll down to "Notifications"
5. Turn on notifications for your account
6. Choose alert style

Android Mail:
1. Open your email app
2. Tap menu → Settings
3. Find "Notifications"
4. Turn on notifications
5. Choose sound/vibration

Android Gmail:
1. Open Gmail
2. Tap menu (three lines)
3. Tap "Settings"
4. Tap your account
5. Tap "Notifications"
6. Turn on notifications

Turning Off Notifications:

If you get too many alerts:
• Reverse the steps above

Customizing:

Different alerts for different:

emailOnPhoneGuide.notificationsTip2: Can be overwhelming - adjust in settings

emailOnPhoneGuide.organizingEmailContent:
Keep your inbox tidy with labels, folders, and search:

Labels (Gmail):

• Archive old emails
• Star important ones for quick access

Folders (Outlook):
• Create custom folders

• Archive when done

Searching:

iPhone:
• Swipe down at top of inbox
• Type what you're looking for
• Find old emails quickly

Android:

Backup:

emailOnPhoneGuide.stayingSecureContent:
A few safety habits to protect your email:

✓ Never reply to suspicious emails asking for passwords
✓ Don't open attachments from people you don't know
✓ If email asks to "confirm information" - it's probably a scam
✓ Never share your password
✓ Log out on shared devices

If You Get a Suspicious Email:
• Don't click any links
• Don't download any attachments
• Mark it as spam or junk
• Delete it
• If unsure, ask library staff
emailOnPhoneGuide.stayingSecureTip2: When in doubt, do not click - ask someone first
emailOnPhoneGuide.troubleshootingLoginContent:
If you can't log in or your app keeps crashing:

Password Wrong Error:

Even though you're sure it's correct:
1. You might have CAPS LOCK on
2. Password might have expired
3. Account might be locked for security
4. Try on a computer first to test password
5. Reset password if needed (see other guide)

App Keeps Crashing:

iPhone:
• Update app (App Store)
• Delete and reinstall app
• Restart phone
• Check storage isn't full

Android:
• Update app (Play Store)
• Delete and reinstall
• Restart phone
• Clear app cache (Settings → Apps)

Still Stuck?
• Ask library staff - we can help with this
• Come in and we'll set it up together
• Or call for phone support
emailOnPhoneGuide.troubleshootingLoginTip1: Passwords expire sometimes - reset if needed
emailOnPhoneGuide.troubleshootingLoginTip3: Library staff can help in person
emailOnPhoneGuide.troubleshootingSyncContent:
If emails won't load or you're not getting notifications:

Emails Won't Download:

iPhone/Android:
1. Check internet connection (WiFi or data)
2. Force-close the app (swipe away)
3. Open app again
4. Wait a few seconds for emails to load
5. If still not working, restart your phone

Stuck on "Loading":
1. Close the app completely
2. Wait 10 seconds
3. Open again
4. Try refreshing/pulling down
5. Check internet connection

Not Getting Notifications:
• Check notifications are ON in settings
• Check notifications aren't muted
• Restart phone
• Delete and reinstall app

Sending Emails Not Working:
1. Check internet is on
2. Tap "Send" again
3. Check email password is correct
4. Delete and reinstall app
5. Try on library computer to test
emailOnPhoneGuide.troubleshootingSyncTip1: Internet connection is required for email
emailOnPhoneGuide.troubleshootingSyncTip2: Restarting the phone fixes most sync issues
emailOnPhoneGuide.troubleshootingSyncTip3: Library WiFi works great for troubleshooting

libraryCardGuide.inPersonApplyContent:
Prefer to apply at the library? Here's how:

What to Bring:
Required:
✓ Valid photo ID (driver's license, passport, etc.)
✓ Proof of current address (utility bill, lease, bank statement)

Helpful (but not required):
✓ Library card number if you had one before
✓ Any ID you might have

At the Library:
1. Go to the front desk
2. Tell staff: "I'd like to get a library card"
3. Staff will:
   - Check your ID
   - Ask you a few questions
   - Create your account on the computer
   - Scan your ID and proof of address
   - Print your library card

You'll walk out with:
• Plastic library card in your hand
• Your library card number
• Ability to borrow, print, and use computers immediately

Time needed: About 10 minutes

Location:
• Main desk (ask any staff member)
• Open during library hours
libraryCardGuide.inPersonApplyTip1: Bring both forms of ID to avoid any delays
libraryCardGuide.inPersonApplyTip2: Staff can answer questions about your account
libraryCardGuide.inPersonApplyTip3: Get your physical card same day
libraryCardGuide.inPersonApplyTip4: Ask about getting your kids cards too

A library card unlocks access to everything at our library:
✓ Borrow books, movies, and music
✓ Use computers and WiFi

libraryCardGuide.introTip2: You'll get your card number immediately
libraryCardGuide.introTip3: Bring ID and proof of address
libraryCardGuide.lostCardContent:
No problem. This is common.

If Your Card is Lost:
1. Tell library staff immediately
2. They'll deactivate it (so no one else uses it)
3. They'll issue you a new one (small fee)
4. You can keep using your library number right away

If Your Card is Damaged:
1. Bring it to the library desk
2. Staff will see if it can be read
3. If not, they'll issue a new one
4. Usually no charge if we damaged it

You can always:
• Call the library to report a lost card
• Use your library number without the card
• Renew items by phone using your number
• Come in anytime to get a replacement

Tip:
• Take a photo of your card and store it on your phone
• Write down your card number somewhere safe
• You don't always need the physical card
libraryCardGuide.lostCardTip1: Call right away if your card is lost - faster service
libraryCardGuide.lostCardTip2: Your library number stays the same forever
libraryCardGuide.lostCardTip3: You can use your number without the physical card
libraryCardGuide.onlineApplyContent:

   - Phone number

5. Click "Submit"

You'll get:
• Instant library card number
• Email confirmation with your number
• Instructions to pick up your physical card

Then:
• Come to the library with ID
• Show your confirmation email
• Get your plastic library card
• You're done.

Most people complete this in 5 minutes online.

libraryCardGuide.onlineApplyTip2: Physical card comes when you pick it up
