passwordResetGuide.gmailNewPasswordContent:
Once verified, Google shows a "Create new password" screen:

1. In the first box: Type a NEW password (not your old one!)
2. In the second box: Type the same password again
3. Your new password should have:
   - At least 8 letters
   - Mix of uppercase and lowercase
   - At least one number
   - At least one special character (!@#$%^&*)
   Example: MyNewPassword123!

4. Click "Change password"
5. You'll see "Password updated"
6. Your password is now reset!
7. You can now log in with your new password
passwordResetGuide.gmailNewPasswordTip1: Save your new password somewhere safe
passwordResetGuide.gmailNewPasswordTip2: You might need to log back into other apps with new password
passwordResetGuide.gmailNewPasswordTip3: Write it down until you memorize it
passwordResetGuide.gmailStartResetContent:
Let's reset your Gmail password. First, start the process:

Step 1: Go to Gmail Login
1. Open your browser
2. Go to: gmail.com
3. You should see the login page
4. Look for "Can't access your account?" or "Forgot password?"

Step 2: Enter Your Email Address
1. When asked, type your full email address
2. Example: jane.smith@gmail.com
3. Click "Next"

Step 3: Enter Your Last Password
1. Gmail asks: "Enter the last password you remember"
2. If you remember ANY old password, enter it
3. If you can't remember any, click "Can't remember password"
4. Click "Next"
passwordResetGuide.gmailStartResetTip1: Have your email address ready before starting
passwordResetGuide.gmailStartResetTip2: Any old password you remember helps - even a guess
passwordResetGuide.gmailVerifyIdentityContent:
Google will ask you to prove it's your account. You'll get ONE of these options:

A) Text Message (Best option!)
   • Select "Send code to your phone"
   • Enter your phone number
   • Get a text with a code
   • Type the code on the screen
   • Click "Verify"

B) Recovery Email
   • If you added a backup email when you created the account
   • Google sends a link to that email
   • Click the link in that email
   • You'll be able to reset your password

C) Security Questions
   • If you set security questions when creating account
   • Answer questions about yourself
   • Click "Next"

Use whichever option Google shows you. If one method doesn't work, click "Try another way" for more options.
passwordResetGuide.gmailVerifyIdentityTip1: Using your phone number is fastest (text verification)
passwordResetGuide.gmailVerifyIdentityTip2: Check your spam folder if you chose recovery email
passwordResetGuide.gmailVerifyIdentityTip3: If nothing works, see the "Recovery Didn't Work" step later
passwordResetGuide.gmailVerifyIdentityTroubleshooting: If you don't get a text or email: 1) Check your spam folder, 2) Try a different recovery method (phone vs email), 3) Ask library staff for help, 4) Try again tomorrow if accounts are locked
passwordResetGuide.introContent:
You can reset your password in a few minutes.

This guide covers:
✓ Resetting your email password (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo)
✓ Resetting your library card PIN
✓ What to do if recovery options don't work
passwordResetGuide.introTip1: You'll need access to your email or phone number you used when creating the account
passwordResetGuide.introTip3: Your account is still secure during this process
passwordResetGuide.libraryPinContent:
Your library card PIN is a 4-digit number (just numbers, no letters):

What It's Used For:
• Checking out items at self-checkout machines
• Phone renewals of books
• Some library computer access

How to Reset It:

Option 1: At the Library Desk
1. Bring your library card (or ID)
2. Go to the main desk
3. Tell staff: "I forgot my PIN"
4. Staff will verify it's your card
5. They'll give you a new PIN on the spot

Option 2: Through Library Website
1. Visit the library's website
2. Log into "My Account"
3. Look for "Manage PIN" or "Change PIN"
4. Follow the steps to reset
5. You might need your card number and birthdate

Your New PIN:
• Will be given to you right away
• Is temporary until you change it to something you'll remember
• You can change it again anytime
• Write it down until you memorize it
passwordResetGuide.libraryPinTip1: Library staff can reset this immediately - it takes 1 minute
passwordResetGuide.libraryPinTip2: Phone number is posted at the library desk
passwordResetGuide.outlookContent:
For Outlook.com or Microsoft accounts:

Step 1: Go to Outlook
1. Visit: outlook.com
2. You should see "Sign in"
3. Look for "Can't access your account?" or "Forgot password?"
4. Click it

Step 2: Enter Email & Solve Puzzle
1. Type your full email address
2. Click "Next"
3. Solve a puzzle to prove you're human
4. Click "Next"

Step 3: How to Verify
Microsoft will ask you to verify. Choose one:

A) Text to Your Phone
   • Select "Text" option
   • Microsoft sends a code via text
   • Type the code they send
   • Click "Verify"

B) Email to Backup Address
   • If you added a backup email
   • Click the link in the recovery email
   • Creates new password

C) Answer Security Questions
   • Questions you set up before
   • Answer them

Step 4: Create New Password
1. Type your new password (at least 8 characters)
2. Mix uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters
3. Confirm by typing it again
4. Click "Next"

Step 5: Done!
1. Your password is reset
2. You can now log into Outlook.com
3. You might need to update password on your phone apps
passwordResetGuide.outlookTip1: Outlook accounts work on Outlook.com and Windows
passwordResetGuide.outlookTip2: You may also have OneDrive and other services linked
passwordResetGuide.pageDescription: Step-by-step help for resetting email or library card passwords
passwordResetGuide.preventFutureContent:
Now that you've reset your password, let's prevent this happening again:

Save Your Password Safely:

Option 1: Password Manager (Recommended)
• Use: Bitwarden, 1Password, LastPass, or Apple Keychain
• They remember passwords for you
• You only need to remember one primary password
• Very secure and convenient

Option 2: Write It Down
• Write in a notebook you keep at home
• Not on a sticky note on your computer!
• Keep it somewhere safe
• This works fine for less important accounts

Option 3: Memorize It
• If it's a strong, simple password
• Say it out loud a few times
• Most people can memorize one main password

Set Up Recovery Options:

1. Add Backup Email
   • Gmail: Settings → Account → Recovery options
   • Outlook: Account.microsoft.com → Security
   • Yahoo: Account → Account security
   • Add another email you have access to
   • Makes recovery easier

2. Add Phone Number
   • Same location as backup email
   • Use a phone number you'll keep
   • They'll text you verification codes

3. Set Security Questions
   • Gmail/Outlook/Yahoo all offer this
   • Use questions with answers ONLY YOU know
   • Avoid public information

4. Create Backup Codes
   • Many services offer one-time backup codes
   • Write these down and keep them safe
   • Use only if you lose access to everything else

Enable 2-Factor Authentication (Extra Security):

What It Is:
• You log in with password
• Service sends you a code (text or app)
• You enter that code
• Makes account much more secure

How to Set Up:
Gmail:
1. Go to myaccount.google.com
2. Click "Security" on left
3. Find "2-Step Verification"
4. Click "Enable"
5. Follow the steps

Outlook:
1. Go to account.microsoft.com/security
2. Click "Advanced security options"
3. Find "Additional security options"
4. Enable 2-Step Verification

This makes your account much safer from hackers!
passwordResetGuide.preventFutureTip1: Password managers are worth the small cost
passwordResetGuide.preventFutureTip2: It takes 5 minutes to set up recovery options
passwordResetGuide.preventFutureTip4: Stronger passwords = less likely to need reset
passwordResetGuide.recoveryFailedContent:
Sometimes password recovery doesn't work. Here's why and what to do:

Common Reasons:
✗ Recovery phone number is old (you got a new phone)
✗ Backup email is outdated
✗ Forgotten security question answers
✗ Account is temporarily locked (for security)
✗ You can't access email or phone on file

What to Try:

1. Wait 24 Hours
   • Sometimes accounts are temporarily locked after failed attempts
   • Try again tomorrow
   • Usually resets within 24 hours

2. Try Different Recovery Method
   • If phone didn't work, try email
   • If email didn't work, try security questions
   • Try all available options

3. Use Another Device
   • Try on a different phone or computer
   • Sometimes device-specific issues cause problems
   • Library computers are available

4. Use Incognito/Private Browsing
   • Open new Incognito or Private window
   • Try password reset again
   • Sometimes cookies cause issues

5. Clear Browser Cache
   Windows:
   • Press: Ctrl + Shift + Delete
   • Select "All time"
   • Clear browsing data

   Mac:
   • Command + Shift + Delete
   • Select "All time"
   • Clear browsing data

6. Ask Google/Microsoft/Yahoo Directly
   For Gmail:
   • Visit: accounts.google.com/account/recovery

   For Outlook:
   • Visit: account.microsoft.com/account/recovery

   For Yahoo:
   • Visit: login.yahoo.com/forgot

What If Nothing Works?

Come visit the library! Our staff can:
✓ Help you step-by-step on library computers
✓ Contact email services on your behalf
✓ Help you create new recovery options
✓ Set up a new email account if needed
✓ Troubleshoot specific error messages
passwordResetGuide.recoveryFailedTip1: Email services prioritize security - resets take time sometimes
passwordResetGuide.recoveryFailedTip2: Library staff have seen this many times
passwordResetGuide.recoveryFailedTip3: Always better to ask for help than to give up
passwordResetGuide.whichPasswordContent:
There are different passwords for different accounts:

Email Password (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo):
• This is what you use to log into your email
• Used when opening Gmail.com, Outlook.com, etc.
• If you forgot this, we help you reset it

Library Card PIN:
• 4-digit number you might use at the library
• Not your account password
• Different from your email password
• Ask staff at the desk if you forgot this

Social Media Passwords (Facebook, Instagram, etc.):
• Login to those websites directly
• Each has its own password reset system

Which one did you forget?
passwordResetGuide.whichPasswordTip1: Most people need help with email passwords
passwordResetGuide.whichPasswordTip2: Library card PINs are much shorter (just numbers)
passwordResetGuide.whichPasswordTip3: Your password and PIN are completely separate
passwordResetGuide.yahooContent:
For Yahoo.com email accounts:

Step 1: Go to Yahoo Login
1. Visit: yahoo.com
2. Click "Sign in"
3. Look for "Trouble signing in?" or "Forgot password?"

Step 2: Verify Your Account
1. Enter your Yahoo email address
2. Click "Next"
3. Yahoo asks you to verify it's really you

You'll be offered options:

A) Verify with Phone
   • Get text with security code
   • Type the code
   • Click "Verify"

B) Verify with Backup Email
   • Confirms using recovery email
   • Click link in that email

C) Account Key
   • If you set one up previously
   • Use that

Step 3: Create New Password
1. Enter your NEW password
2. Confirm it by typing again
3. Password needs: 8+ characters, mix of cases, numbers, special characters
4. Click "Save changes"

Step 4: Log In
1. Go to Yahoo.com
2. Use your new password to sign in
3. You're done!
passwordResetGuide.yahooTip1: Yahoo has lots of security options - use whichever is easiest
passwordResetGuide.yahooTip2: Your Yahoo account may have other services attached

scamRecognitionGuide.description: Learn how to spot common scams and protect yourself online
scamRecognitionGuide.emailScamsPhishingContent:
Phishing emails try to trick you into revealing passwords or personal info.

What They Look Like:
[WARNING] "Confirm your password"
[WARNING] "Verify your account"
[WARNING] "Unusual activity on your account"
[WARNING] "Update your payment information"
[WARNING] "Click here to claim prize"

Red Flags:
[FLAG] Urgent language ("ACT NOW!" "IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED")
[FLAG] Asking for passwords or personal info
[FLAG] Mismatched email address (looks official but isn't)
[FLAG] Bad grammar or spelling
[FLAG] Link doesn't match the sender name
[FLAG] Generic greeting ("Dear Customer" instead of your name)
[FLAG] Suspicious attachments

Example:
"From: PayPal Security Team
Subject: URGENT - Unusual activity detected!
Message: Click here to confirm your identity

Your account has been locked.
Click: www.paypall-security.com (NOT real PayPal!)
Enter your password to unlock."

What to Do:
• Don't click the link
• Don't reply to the email
• Close the email
• Go directly to the real website (not the link)
• Report the email as spam/phishing
• Delete the email

How to Report:
Gmail: Click "Report phishing"
Outlook: Click "Junk" → "Phishing"
Other: Forward to phishing@company.com
scamRecognitionGuide.emailScamsPhishingTip1: Real companies never ask for passwords in emails
scamRecognitionGuide.emailScamsPhishingTip2: Go directly to the official website, never click email links
scamRecognitionGuide.emailScamsPhishingTip3: Hover over links to see the real address (don't click)
scamRecognitionGuide.emailScamsPhishingTip4: When in doubt, call the company directly
scamRecognitionGuide.emailScamsPhishingTroubleshooting: If you clicked a link: Change your password immediately and monitor your account for fraud.
scamRecognitionGuide.howToProtectYourselfContent:
Best Practices:

Passwords:
• Use strong passwords (8+ characters, mix of letters/numbers/symbols)
• Different password for each account
• Password manager (like Bitwarden) remembers them for you
• Never share passwords

Two-Factor Authentication:
• Enable on email, social media, bank accounts
• Even if they get your password, they can't access your account
• Takes extra 10 seconds but protects you

Email & Online:
• Don't open attachments from strangers
• Hover over links to see real address (don't click)
• Check sender address carefully
• If unsure, go directly to website

Shopping Online:
• Only use secure websites (look for padlock icon)
• Only use trusted retailers
• Keep receipts and confirmation emails
• Monitor credit card statements

Phone Calls:
• Don't give info to unsolicited callers
• Hang up and call back using official number
• Banks will never call asking for passwords
• Real support can wait - you call them

General Safety:
• Keep software/apps updated
• Use antivirus (Windows Defender, Malwarebytes)
• Be skeptical - if weird, question it
• Talk to trusted people about suspicious things
• When in doubt, ask a librarian!

What NOT to Do:
[WARNING] Don't share passwords via email
[WARNING] Don't use WiFi without VPN for banking
[WARNING] Don't save passwords in browser
[WARNING] Don't ignore security warnings
[WARNING] Don't trust caller ID (easily spoofed)
[WARNING] Don't click links in unexpected emails
[WARNING] Don't enable remote access for strangers
scamRecognitionGuide.howToProtectYourselfTip1: Most scams are preventable with caution
scamRecognitionGuide.howToProtectYourselfTip2: Your library staff can help with online safety
scamRecognitionGuide.howToProtectYourselfTip3: Teaching others helps protect your community
scamRecognitionGuide.ifYouSuspectAScamContent:
Follow these steps if you think something is a scam:

Step 1: STOP
[WARNING] Don't send money
[WARNING] Don't click links
[WARNING] Don't download anything
[WARNING] Don't give personal info

Step 2: VERIFY
Call the organization directly using a number from their official website
(Not a number from the email/message)

Step 3: REPORT
Report to:
• Email provider (Gmail, Outlook, etc.)
• Social media platform
• Website/organization
• FTC (ftc.gov)
• FBI (ic3.gov)
• Local police (non-emergency)

Step 4: TELL SOMEONE
Tell trusted friends/family so they're aware too

If Money Was Sent:

Immediately:
1. Contact your bank/payment service
2. Tell them you were scammed
3. Ask about reversing the transaction
4. Report stolen payment method
5. File a police report

Then:
• Change all your passwords
• Monitor credit cards for fraud
• Consider credit freeze (protects against ID theft)
• Don't be embarrassed - this happens to millions

Reporting Resources:
• FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center: ic3.gov
• FTC Scam Report: reportfraud.ftc.gov
• Local police: Non-emergency number
• Your bank's fraud department

Important:
Scammers are good at what they do. If you fell for one, it's not your fault. Millions of smart people fall for scams every year.

The important thing is:
• Recognize it as fraud
• Stop engaging
• Tell authorities
• Help protect others by sharing
scamRecognitionGuide.ifYouSuspectAScamTip1: Money rarely can be recovered once sent
scamRecognitionGuide.ifYouSuspectAScamTip2: Act fast if money was already sent
scamRecognitionGuide.ifYouSuspectAScamTip3: Keep all emails and messages as evidence
scamRecognitionGuide.introContent:
Scammers are clever and try to trick millions of people every day.
You can protect yourself by knowing what to look for.

This guide teaches you:
• How to recognize common scams
• What to do if you see one
• How to report scams
• How to stay safe online
scamRecognitionGuide.introTip1: Scams target everyone - young and old
scamRecognitionGuide.introTip2: If something feels wrong, it probably is
scamRecognitionGuide.introTip3: Never feel embarrassed if you almost fell for one
scamRecognitionGuide.introTip4: Telling others helps protect them too
scamRecognitionGuide.moneyTransferPrizeScamsContent:
These scammers claim you won something or have money waiting, but need to send money first.

"You Won!" Scams:
[WARNING] "You won a prize!" (you never entered)
[WARNING] "Claim your inheritance" (from unknown relative)
[WARNING] "Congratulations - lottery winner!" (didn't buy ticket)
[WARNING] "Free money from government"

They Always Ask:
• Processing fee
• Tax payment upfront
• ID verification fee
• Wire transfer of funds
• Gift cards or cryptocurrency

The Reality:
• Real prizes don't require money first
• Actual lotteries don't notify by email
• Government benefits don't work this way
• You never have to pay to get free money
• Legitimate contests are verified

What to Do:
• Delete or ignore the message
• Don't respond or click links
• If unsure, call the organization directly
• Report the message
• Tell others

Example Scams:
1. "You won $500,000 in Microsoft Lottery!"
   → You never entered a Microsoft Lottery

2. "Claim your $1,200 stimulus check"
   → Government doesn't email about benefits

3. "You inherited money from a relative"
   → From someone you've never heard of

4. "Free government grant for small business"
   → Legitimate grants don't work this way
scamRecognitionGuide.moneyTransferPrizeScamsTip1: If it sounds too good to be true, it is
scamRecognitionGuide.moneyTransferPrizeScamsTip2: Real organizations have websites you can verify
scamRecognitionGuide.moneyTransferPrizeScamsTip4: Call organizations directly using phone book number
scamRecognitionGuide.romanceDatingScamsContent:
Scammers create fake profiles to build relationships and then ask for money.

What They Look Like:
[WARNING] Too-good-to-be-true profile pictures
[WARNING] Person immediately says "I love you"
[WARNING] Quick progression to meeting/marriage talk
[WARNING] Then asks for money ("emergency back home")
[WARNING] Asks for gift cards or wire transfer

Red Flags:
[FLAG] Won't video chat (always excuses)
[FLAG] Asks for money very soon in relationship
[FLAG] Says they're stuck abroad needing rescue
[FLAG] Claims family emergency needing funds
[FLAG] Asks you to keep relationship secret
[FLAG] Profile looks like a model/celebrity
[FLAG] Lives conveniently far away

Common Excuses:
"I need money for plane ticket to see you"
"My mother needs surgery"
"I'm stuck at airport"
"Business emergency - need $5,000"

What to Do:
• Ask for video chat - real people will
• Do a reverse image search (Google Images)
• Ask personal questions (memory from past conversations)
• Don't send money - EVER
• Tell trusted friends/family about concerns
• Report the profile

If You've Been Scammed:
• Tell your bank immediately
• Report to the dating app
• Report to FBI (ic3.gov)
• Tell someone you trust
• Don't feel ashamed - it happens to thousands
scamRecognitionGuide.romanceDatingScamsTip1: Real relationships don't require money from strangers
scamRecognitionGuide.romanceDatingScamsTip2: Video chat early if it's getting serious
scamRecognitionGuide.romanceDatingScamsTip3: Google image search photos to verify identity
scamRecognitionGuide.romanceDatingScamsTip4: Trust your gut - if weird, it probably is
scamRecognitionGuide.socialMediaScamsContent:
Scammers use Facebook, Instagram, and other social media to target people.

Common Social Media Scams:

Friend/Family Impersonation:
"Hi Mom! I'm stuck in Mexico and need $1,000 for hotel!"
Reality: Usually someone hacked their account or it's a fake profile

What to Do:
• Call your friend/family to verify
• Ask personal questions only they'd know
• Don't send money via social media
• Tell the platform it's impersonation

Fake Giveaways:
"Like and share to win an iPhone!"
Reality: You'll get hacked or spam, never the prize

Fake Jobs:
"Make $5,000/week from home!"
Reality: They'll ask for money upfront or your info

Marketplace Scams:
Selling something on Facebook/Craigslist?
[WARNING] Paying in gift cards
[WARNING] Overpaying and asking you to wire back difference
[WARNING] Meeting in unsafe location
[WARNING] No payment verification

What to Do:
• Meet in safe public place (police station parking lot)
• Bring someone with you
• Verify payment before handing over item
• Use secure payment methods
• Tell someone where you're going

Red Flags on Social Media:
[FLAG] Account brand new (few friends/followers)
[FLAG] Few or stolen photos
[FLAG] Messages with poor grammar
[FLAG] Quick trust-building
[FLAG] Requests to move to private messaging
scamRecognitionGuide.socialMediaScamsTip1: Don't click suspicious links on social media
scamRecognitionGuide.socialMediaScamsTip2: Verify friend requests from people you know
scamRecognitionGuide.socialMediaScamsTip3: Never send money through social media
scamRecognitionGuide.techSupportScamsContent:
These scammers pretend to be tech support and trick you into giving access to your computer.

What They Look Like:
[WARNING] "Your computer has a virus - call now!"
[WARNING] Pop-up saying "System Error - Contact Tech Support"
[WARNING] Pop-up with phone number to call
[WARNING] Email saying you have malware
[WARNING] Caller claiming to be from Apple, Microsoft, or your bank

Red Flags:
[FLAG] Unsolicited call or message
[FLAG] They want remote access to your computer
[FLAG] They ask you to download something
[FLAG] They want payment for "fixing" the problem
[FLAG] They ask for credit card information
[FLAG] Pop-ups claiming urgent action needed

Example:
"WARNING: VIRUS DETECTED!
Your computer is at risk!
Call 1-800-555-0199 immediately
Or download antivirus software"

The Reality:
• Your browser can't detect viruses in pop-ups
• Apple/Microsoft/Banks don't call randomly
• Real tech support doesn't ask for remote access
• They don't demand immediate payment
• Real software never pops up with urgency

What to Do:
• Don't call the number
• Don't download anything
• Close the browser tab or window
• Restart your computer if needed
• Ignore pop-up messages
• Report the pop-up (right-click → Report)

If You Already Did:
• Change your passwords immediately
• Check your credit card for fraud
• Run a real antivirus scan (Windows Defender, Malwarebytes)
• Tell your bank about any credit card activity
• Consider calling a real tech expert
scamRecognitionGuide.techSupportScamsTip1: Real tech support never calls you first
scamRecognitionGuide.techSupportScamsTip2: If your computer acts up, call YOUR provider directly
scamRecognitionGuide.techSupportScamsTip3: Close pop-ups without clicking anything inside
scamRecognitionGuide.techSupportScamsTip4: Library staff can help check your computer
scamRecognitionGuide.youreNowMoreAwareContent:
You now know how to recognize and avoid common scams!

Remember:
• If it feels wrong, it probably is
• Real organizations don't ask for passwords
• Money sent can't usually be recovered
• You're not alone - millions get targeted
• Reporting scams helps others

Quick Reference:
- Phishing Emails: Don't click, report
- Tech Support: Don't download, don't call
- Romance: Video chat, verify identity
- Money "Offers": Never send money first
- Social Media: Verify before trusting
- Any Scam: Report it!

If Something Seems Wrong:
1. Trust your instinct
2. Ask a trusted person
3. Go directly to official sources
4. Never send money to verify
5. Report if it's fraud

Resources:
• Scam alert website: fbi.gov/scams-safety
• FTC fraud report: reportfraud.ftc.gov
• Your library staff - we can help!
• Trusted friends and family

Stay safe online!
scamRecognitionGuide.youreNowMoreAwareTip2: Share this knowledge with friends and family
scamRecognitionGuide.youreNowMoreAwareTip3: If you spot a scam, help others avoid it
scamRecognitionGuide.youreNowMoreAwareTip4: Library staff can help answer safety questions

wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepCheckYourDistanceFrom: Step 1: Check Your Distance from WiFi
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepMoveCloserOrSwitch: Step 3: Move Closer or Switch Networks
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepWhenToAskFor: Step 4: When to Ask for Help
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.wifiAsksForPasswordOr: WiFi asks for password or won\
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.wifiIsConnectedButVery: WiFi is connected but very slow
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.beforeYouStartChecklist:
Before you start, make sure:
• Your device is charged and turned on
• You are inside or near the library building
• You know your device type (phone, tablet, laptop)
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.optionCantSeeWifiNetworkAtAll: I can't see the WiFi network at all
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.optionWifiAsksForPasswordOrWontConnect: WiFi asks for password or won't connect
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.pageSubtitle: Can't connect or connection keeps dropping? Start here.
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.quickFixTip1: Turn WiFi OFF and back ON (wait 10 seconds)
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.quickFixTip3: Move closer to the library's main area
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.quickFixTip4: Ask staff for the WiFi network name and password
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.quickFixTip5: Check if airplane mode is turned OFF
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepCheckWhatYoureRunningContent:
Other apps using WiFi can slow everything down:

Close Unnecessary Apps:

iPhone/iPad:
• Look for apps using WiFi in the background
• Swipe up from bottom to close apps
• Especially: Video apps, cloud sync, social media

Android:
• Open Settings → Apps
• Check which apps use WiFi background data
• Go back and force-close heavy apps

Windows/Laptop:
• Look at taskbar for heavy apps
• Close web browsers with many tabs
• Pause cloud backup (OneDrive, Google Drive, iCloud)
• Close video/streaming apps

Try these solutions:
• Close web browser tabs you're not using
• Pause cloud backup during your visit
• Turn off video autoplay in social media
• Close background apps
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepCheckWhatYoureRunningTip1: One streaming video uses as much bandwidth as 50 people browsing
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepCheckWhatYoureRunningTip2: Cloud sync (OneDrive, iCloud) runs in background
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepCheckYourConnectionSpeedContent:
First, confirm the WiFi is actually slow:

Quick Speed Test (requires already connected):
• Open your browser on the library computers
• Visit: speedtest.net
• Click "GO"
• Wait for results

What's "normal" library WiFi:
• Download: 5-25 Mbps (reasonable for library)
• Upload: 1-5 Mbps
• Below 5 Mbps = slow

If slow:
• Note the speed number
• Tell library staff (helps them troubleshoot)
• May indicate a network issue, not your device

Try these solutions:
• Check peak vs. off-peak times (mornings usually faster)
• Report speeds below 2 Mbps to staff
• Use library computers for critical tasks
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepCheckYourConnectionSpeedTip1: Speed varies based on how many people are online
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepCheckYourConnectionSpeedTip2: Video streaming needs at least 2-3 Mbps
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepCheckYourDistanceFromContent:
WiFi strength weakens with distance. Your device might be too far away:

Signs You're Too Far:
• WiFi shows only 1-2 bars
• Other devices stay connected when you move
• Connection drops in certain parts of the library

What to do:
• Move closer to the library center
• Ask staff where the nearest access point is
• Try sitting in a different area
• Move away from walls and doors

Try these solutions:
• Relocate to a different area of the library
• Move closer to windows or public areas
• Move at least 10-15 feet away from outer walls
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepCheckYourDistanceFromTip1: WiFi range is usually 30-50 feet in open areas
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepCheckYourDistanceFromTip2: Walls cut range in half or more
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepConfirmLookingInRightPlace: Step 2: Confirm You're Looking in the Right Place
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepConfirmLookingInRightPlaceContent:
WiFi networks appear in a list. Make sure you're looking at the complete list:

Windows:
• Click the WiFi icon in the bottom right
• A popup shows all available networks
• Scroll down if list is long
• Look for networks starting with "LSC_" or "Library"

iPhone/iPad:
• Go to Settings → WiFi
• Wait a few seconds for the full list to load
• Look for networks with "LSC_" or "Library" in the name

Android:
• Go to Settings → Network & Internet → WiFi
• Tap "See all" if you don't see many networks
• Look for networks starting with "LSC_" or "Library"

Try these solutions:
• Move closer to a library WiFi access point (near windows, public areas)
• Wait 30 seconds for the network list to fully load
• Scroll down in the network list - may be below other networks
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepConfirmLookingInRightPlaceTip1: The library has multiple access points - you might see LSC_1, LSC_2, LSC_3, etc.
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepConfirmLookingInRightPlaceTip2: Choose the one with the strongest signal (full bars)
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepConfirmWifiIsEnabledContent:
Make sure your device's WiFi is turned on:

Windows or Laptop:
• Look for a WiFi icon in the bottom right corner
• It should show a WiFi symbol (looks like curved lines)
• If grayed out, click it to turn WiFi ON

iPhone or iPad:
• Swipe down from top-right corner to open Control Center
• Look for the WiFi icon (looks like curved lines)
• If it's not filled in, tap it to turn WiFi ON

Android Phone:
• Swipe down twice to open full Quick Settings
• Find "WiFi" button
• Tap it if it's off (should turn blue when on)

Try these solutions:
• Turn WiFi off and back on (wait 10 seconds)
• Restart your device completely
• Check if airplane mode is ON - turn it OFF
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepConfirmWifiIsEnabledTip1: WiFi symbols are the same on all devices - curved lines
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepConfirmWifiIsEnabledTip2: Airplane mode blocks all wireless - disable it first
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepEnterPasswordCorrectlyContent:
When connecting, carefully enter the password:

iPhone/iPad:
• Select the WiFi network
• Tap "Connect"
• When asked for password, type it exactly
• Check CAPS LOCK - often the problem!
• Tap "Connect"

Android:
• Select the WiFi network
• Tap "Connect"
• Enter password in the "Password" field
• Check that CAPS LOCK is OFF
• Tap "Connect"

Windows/Laptop:
• Right-click WiFi icon → Select network
• Click "Connect" on your network
• Enter password exactly as written
• Check for CAPS LOCK
• Click "OK"

Try these solutions:
• Copy/paste the password if possible to avoid typos
• Clear the field and re-enter it slowly
• Check if CAPS LOCK key is on - turn it OFF
• Make sure you're on "LSC_Public" or the right network
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepEnterPasswordCorrectlyTip1: One wrong character and it won't connect
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepEnterPasswordCorrectlyTip2: If unsure about capitals, ask staff to write it down
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepForgetAndReconnectContent:
Sometimes your device "remembers" an incorrect password. Forget the network and try again:

iPhone/iPad:
• Go to Settings → WiFi
• Find "LSC_Public" (or your network)
• Tap the info button (a small letter i in a circle)
• Tap "Forget This Network"
• Then reconnect and enter password fresh

Android:
• Go to Settings → WiFi
• Long-press the network name
• Tap "Forget" or "Remove"
• Reconnect and enter password again

Windows:
• Right-click WiFi icon → Open Network settings
• Find "Manage known networks"
• Find your network and click "Forget"
• Reconnect and re-enter password
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepForgetAndReconnectTroubleshooting: Forgetting clears the "memory" of wrong passwords. Restart your device after forgetting and reconnecting. You can also try a different WiFi network as a test. Your device saves passwords - sometimes the old one is stuck. Forgetting fixes 60% of connection problems.
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepGetTheCorrectPasswordContent:
Our library WiFi might require a password. Here's how to get it:

Getting the Password:
• Ask any library staff member at the desk
• Password is usually posted at the front desk on a sign
• It may be on your library card receipt
• Staff can also provide it by phone

Common Password Hints:
• Usually includes the library name
• May have numbers
• Case-sensitive (UPPERCASE different from lowercase)
• No spaces typically

Try these solutions:
• Visit the front desk and ask for WiFi password
• Call the library and ask (staff will provide it)
• Check your library card receipt if you got one today
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepGetTheCorrectPasswordTip1: Write down the password - you'll need it to reconnect
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepGetTheCorrectPasswordTip2: Different networks might have different passwords
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepMoveCloserOrSwitchContent:
WiFi strength affects speed:

If Connection is Weak:
• Move closer to the library center
• Find an area with 4-5 WiFi bars showing
• Move away from walls
• Try a different area entirely

Check Network Quality:

iPhone/iPad:
• Settings → WiFi
• Look at the number of bars next to the network name
• 4-5 bars = good speed
• 1-2 bars = slow

Android:
• Settings → WiFi
• Same - more bars = faster

Strength matters:
• At 1-2 bars: expect slow speeds
• At 4-5 bars: should be much faster

Try these solutions:
• Relocate to a stronger signal area
• Ask staff for the best spot to sit
• Try again during less busy hours
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepMoveCloserOrSwitchTip1: Just because you're connected doesn't mean you have good signal
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepMoveCloserOrSwitchTip2: Moving 10 feet can make a huge difference
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepMoveCloserToTheContent:
WiFi has range limits - closer is better!

Where to try:
• Near the main desk area
• In the computer lab
• By the windows
• In the public seating areas

What to avoid:
• Restrooms (no WiFi coverage)
• Storage areas (signal blocked by materials)
• Outer walls (weaker signal outside)
• Basement areas (if signal doesn't reach there)

Try these solutions:
• Walk around the library finding areas with good reception
• Ask staff "Where has the strongest WiFi?" - they know!
• Look for other patrons on devices - usually good signal there
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepMoveCloserToTheTip1: Concrete, brick, and many books block WiFi signals
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepMoveCloserToTheTip2: Metal objects and microwaves can interfere with WiFi
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepReduceWifiInterferenceContent:
Other wireless devices can interfere with WiFi:

Common Interference Sources:
• Microwave ovens (very strong interference!)
• Bluetooth devices very close by
• Cordless phones
• Baby monitors
• Radio stations
• Many devices on same WiFi network

What to do:
• Move away from the library kitchen area
• Turn off Bluetooth if you're not using it
• Move away from other people using WiFi heavily
• Suggest to staff if a microwave is near computers

Try these solutions:
• Disable Bluetooth when not needed
• Move to a different room away from kitchen
• Ask staff if they can help identify interference
• Suggest that staff check WiFi channel settings (5GHz vs 2.4GHz)
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepReduceWifiInterferenceTip1: Microwaves are notorious for WiFi interference
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepReduceWifiInterferenceTip2: Bluetooth headphones/mice can interfere if too close
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepResetNetworkSettingsLastContent:
If nothing else works, reset your WiFi settings:

iPhone/iPad:
• Go to Settings → General → Reset
• Tap "Reset Network Settings"
• Your device will restart
• Reconnect to WiFi (you'll need the password)

Android:
• Go to Settings → System → Reset
• Tap "Reset WiFi, mobile & Bluetooth"
• Confirm when asked
• Reconnect to WiFi

Windows:
• Right-click WiFi icon → Open Network settings
• Scroll down to "Advanced network settings"
• Click "Network reset"
• Restart your device
• Reconnect to WiFi
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepResetNetworkSettingsLastTip1: Only do this if other steps don't work
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepResetNetworkSettingsLastTip2: You'll need all your WiFi passwords handy after doing this
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepResetNetworkSettingsLastTroubleshoot: This removes all saved WiFi networks and resets settings. You'll need to re-enter passwords for all networks. Only do this if other steps don't work - you'll need all your WiFi passwords handy after doing this.
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepUpdateYourDeviceContent:
Outdated software can cause WiFi problems:

Check for Updates:

iPhone/iPad:
• Go to Settings → General → Software Update
• If an update is available, tap "Download and Install"
• Keep device plugged in during update

Android:
• Go to Settings → System → System Update
• Tap "Check for updates"
• If available, tap "Download and install"

Windows/Laptop:
• Click Start → Settings → Update & Security
• Click "Check for updates"
• Install any available updates

Try these solutions:
• Install the latest software updates
• Restart your device after updating
• Once updated, "forget" and reconnect to WiFi
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepUpdateYourDeviceTip1: Updates often fix WiFi stability problems
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepUpdateYourDeviceTip2: Set updates to automatic if possible
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepWhenToAskForContent:
If speed is still poor after these steps:

Tell staff:
• "I'm getting 2-3 Mbps on the WiFi"
• Or "My WiFi keeps dropping when I move around"
• Or "WiFi works but videos won't play"

What staff can check:
• Network load (how many people are online)
• WiFi channel interference
• Your device's compatibility
• Whether it's a device problem or network problem

Next steps might be:
• Use a library computer instead
• Come back during quieter hours
• Get help with specific tasks
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepWhenToAskForTip1: Describing the problem clearly helps staff solve it faster
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepWhenToAskForTip2: Speed varies throughout the day - early morning usually fastest
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.stepWhenToAskForTroubleshooting: Staff can identify if it's a device or network issue. They may suggest using library computers instead. They can also escalate to IT if the network is actually down. Describing the problem clearly helps staff solve it faster. Speed varies throughout the day - early morning is usually fastest.
wiFiTroubleshootingGuide.wifiAsksForPasswordOrConnectionFails: WiFi Asks for Password or Connection Fails

wirelessPrintingGuide.stepLocateAndSelectA: Step 2: Locate and Select a Printer
wirelessPrintingGuide.advancedPrintingFromCloudServicesContent:
You can also print documents stored online:

From Google Drive:
1. Open your document in Google Drive
2. Click File → Print
3. Select your library printer
4. Click Print

From OneDrive/Office:
1. Open your document in Office Online
2. Click File → Print
3. Select your library printer
4. Click Print

From Email Attachments:
1. Open the attachment in your email
2. Tap the Share/Print icon
3. Select your library printer
4. Confirm and print
wirelessPrintingGuide.advancedPrintingFromCloudServicesTip1: You can print from any cloud service that supports printing
wirelessPrintingGuide.advancedPrintingFromCloudServicesTip2: Keep passwords private - don't let others access your cloud accounts at library computers
wirelessPrintingGuide.advancedPrintingFromCloudServicesTip3: Larger files may take a few extra seconds to process
wirelessPrintingGuide.description: Learn how to print from your device using our wireless printing service
wirelessPrintingGuide.introContent:
Wireless printing allows you to print documents from your device without needing cables. This guide will walk you through connecting to our library's wireless printers.

Before you start, you will need:
• A charged device (phone, tablet, or laptop)
• The document or webpage you want to print
• Connection to the library WiFi network
wirelessPrintingGuide.introTip1: Make sure your device is charged before starting
wirelessPrintingGuide.introTip2: You'll need to be connected to the library WiFi network
wirelessPrintingGuide.introTip3: Printers are available in the computer lab and reference areas
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepCollectYourPrintoutContent:
Your document is ready!

1. Head to the printer location (check the printer name for location)
2. Look for your document in the output tray
3. If using paid printing, your page may be held at the desk
4. Pay the cashier if you haven't already set up an account

That's it! You've successfully printed wirelessly.
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepCollectYourPrintoutTip1: Keep printouts organized - staff will discard unclaimed prints after 2 weeks
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepCollectYourPrintoutTip2: If you print multiple jobs, check all output trays
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepCollectYourPrintoutTip3: Ask staff if you need help finding your document
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepConnectToLibraryWifiContent:
First, connect your device to the library WiFi network:

1. Open your device's WiFi settings
2. Look for network names starting with "LSC_" or "Library"
3. Select "LSC_Public" or the available library network
4. If prompted, enter the password posted at the library desk
5. Wait for a "Connected" confirmation
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepConnectToLibraryWifiTip1: WiFi networks are available throughout the building
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepConnectToLibraryWifiTip2: You may see multiple library networks - choose the strongest signal
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepConnectToLibraryWifiTroubleshooting: If you can't connect: 1) Restart your device's WiFi, 2) Move closer to a WiFi access point, 3) Ask staff for the current WiFi password
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepLocateAndSelectAContent:
Now you'll add the printer to your device:

For Windows:
1. Open Settings → Devices → Printers & Scanners
2. Click "Add a printer or scanner"
3. Wait for the library printers to appear
4. Select "LSC_Library_Printer_Main" from the list
5. Click "Add device"

For Mac:
1. Click the Apple menu → System Settings → Printers & Scanners
2. Click the "+" button
3. Select the "Windows/Samba" printer option
4. Enter: smb://LSC_Library_Printer_Main
5. Click "Add"

For Mobile Devices:
1. Open Settings → Bluetooth & Device Connection → Printers
2. Select "LSC_Library_Printer_Mobile"
3. Follow the pairing prompts
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepLocateAndSelectATip1: Printer names usually indicate their location (Main, Lab, Front Desk)
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepLocateAndSelectATip2: Make sure you select the printer that's closest to you
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepLocateAndSelectATroubleshooting: If printer doesn't appear: 1) Ensure WiFi is connected, 2) Restart your device, 3) Forget and reconnect to WiFi
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepPrintATestDocumentContent:
Let's print a test page to confirm everything works:

1. Open any document or photo on your device
2. Look for a "Share" or "Print" button (usually in the File menu)
3. Select your printer from the list
4. Choose:
   - Copies: 1
   - Color: Black & White (saves money!)
   - Paper size: Letter (8.5" x 11")
5. Tap or click "Print"
6. Your document should print within 30 seconds
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepPrintATestDocumentTip1: Black & white printing costs $0.10 per page
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepPrintATestDocumentTip2: Color printing is available but costs more
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepPrintATestDocumentTip3: Check that you're printing to the right printer before confirming
wirelessPrintingGuide.stepPrintATestDocumentTroubleshooting: If nothing prints: 1) Check the printer display to see if there's an error, 2) Ask staff to help troubleshoot, 3) Try printing from a different application
wirelessPrintingGuide.youreAllSetContent:
All done. You now know how to use wireless printing at the library.

Quick Reference:
• WiFi Network: LSC_Public
• Main Printer: LSC_Library_Printer_Main
• Black & White: $0.10 per page
• Ask for help: Reference Desk or Tech Help Area

Come back anytime if you need help!
wirelessPrintingGuide.youreAllSetTip1: Bookmark this guide for future reference
wirelessPrintingGuide.youreAllSetTip2: Printers are available during all library hours
wirelessPrintingGuide.youreAllSetTip3: Staff members are always available to help

libraryCards.title: Library Cards & Accounts
libraryCards.description: Getting started with your library membership

0.question: How do I get a library card?
0.quickAnswer: Bring ID + proof of address. Free for residents. Options available if no fixed address.

1.question: What if I don't have a permanent address?
1.quickAnswer: You can still get a card! Use a shelter, agency letter, or the library address.

2.question: Can I get a library card if I don't live in the service area?
2.quickAnswer: Yes! $50/year, or free if you live in Elmdale or Thornbury.

3.question: How do I replace a lost library card?
3.quickAnswer: $2 fee. Bring photo ID to the desk.

4.question: Can children get their own library card?
4.quickAnswer: Yes, any age! Under 14 needs parent signature. Parents can see checkouts and holds.

5.question: What happens when my card expires?
5.quickAnswer: Renewing is free and easy. Your holds and account data are never lost.

6.question: What's the difference between a library card and an online account?
6.quickAnswer: The card gives you borrowing privileges. The account lets you manage holds, renewals, and digital resources online.

7.question: Do I need to wait for my card to be approved before creating an account?
7.quickAnswer: No! Create your account anytime. Link your card later when it's approved.

8.question: How do I update my contact information?
8.quickAnswer: Email/phone: update online. Address: visit in person.

borrowing.title: Borrowing & Returns
borrowing.description: Loan periods, renewals, and returning items

0.question: What are the loan periods?
0.quickAnswer: Books: 3 weeks. DVDs: 1 week. Magazines: 2 weeks.

1.question: How do I renew items?
1.quickAnswer: Online, by phone, app, or in person. Up to 2 renewals.

2.question: What happens if I return items late?
2.quickAnswer: No daily fines! But 30+ days late = replacement charge.

3.question: Do you offer interlibrary loan?
3.quickAnswer: Yes! Free for books, 1-2 weeks to arrive.

4.question: Can I return items to any branch?
4.quickAnswer: Yes! Return anywhere, we handle the rest.

5.question: How do I place a hold on an item?
5.quickAnswer: Search catalog, click 'Place Hold', we'll notify you.

7.question: Will I lose my place in the hold queue?
7.quickAnswer: No! Your spot is saved automatically until the item is available.

8.question: What happens if I lose or damage an item?
8.quickAnswer: You will be charged the replacement cost. Return the item and the charge goes away.

network.offline:
It looks like we've lost our connection. Here's what you can try:
1. Check that your WiFi or internet is connected
2. Refresh the page
3. Wait a moment and try again

If you're still having trouble, stop by the library - we're happy to help!
network.timeout: This is taking longer than expected. The library's servers might be busy right now. Would you mind trying again in a moment?
network.serverUnavailable: Our system is taking a quick break right now. We're working on it! Please try again in a few minutes.

auth.loginFailed: Hmm, we couldn't find that combination. Double-check your email and password? If you've forgotten your password, the 'Forgot Password' link can help you get back in.
auth.cardLoginFailed: We couldn't match that library card and PIN. Take a moment to double-check both - your card number starts with {{cardPrefix}} followed by 6 digits (like {{cardPrefix}}123456).
auth.registrationFailed:
We weren't able to create your account just yet. This usually happens when:
- The email address is already in use
- The password doesn't meet our requirements
- There's a connection hiccup

Give it another try, and if it's still not working, stop by the library - we're here to help.
auth.sessionExpired: Your session has timed out for security. No worries - just sign in again and you'll be right back where you were!
auth.accountLocked: For your security, we've temporarily locked this account after several login attempts. You can try again in 30 minutes, or stop by the library and we'll help sort it out.
auth.rateLimited: Whoa, that's a lot of attempts! Let's take a 5-minute breather, then try again. If you're having trouble remembering your password, the 'Forgot Password' link is there for you.
auth.invalidCredentials: Hmm, we couldn't find that combination. Double-check your email and password? If you've forgotten your password, the 'Forgot Password' link can help you get back in.

accessibilityPage.acknowledgmentValue: We will acknowledge your grievance within 2 business days of receiving it.
accessibilityPage.alternativeFormatsValue: This procedure, and any library information, is available in large print or other accessible formats on request.
accessibilityPage.appealsValue: If the Coordinator's response does not resolve the matter, you may appeal in writing to the Library Director within 15 business days. If the Director's decision still does not resolve it, you may appeal to the Library Board, which meets the third Tuesday of each month at 6:30 p.m.
accessibilityPage.changeSiteLooksPrompt: Looking to change how this site looks and feels?
accessibilityPage.committedToEnsuring: {{libraryName}} is committed to ensuring that our services, facilities, and digital resources are accessible to all members of our community.
accessibilityPage.conformanceStatusValue: Partially conformant — the L30 platform substantially meets WCAG 2.1 AA. Known gaps are documented below and tracked in our public issue queue.
accessibilityPage.digital4: Text resizing without loss of functionality
accessibilityPage.equitableGoalText: Our goal is to provide an equitable experience for all patrons, regardless of ability.
accessibilityPage.evaluationMethodValue: Automated axe-core scans on every public page in our test suite, plus manual keyboard, screen-reader (NVDA, VoiceOver), and color-contrast review. Third-party audit not yet commissioned; available on request.
accessibilityPage.feedbackIntro: We want to hear from you about accessibility. Please tell us if you encounter barriers such as: website difficult to read, confusing instructions, missing video captions, buttons too small to click, or staff not understanding your accessibility needs. Contact us:
accessibilityPage.feedbackResponseTime: We respond to accessibility feedback within 2 business days (Monday through Friday). If we cannot fix the issue immediately, we will explain what we are doing and when you can expect a solution.
accessibilityPage.filingGrievanceRightsText: Filing a grievance with the library does not affect your right to file a complaint with the U.S. Department of Justice or to pursue other remedies available under the ADA.
accessibilityPage.forSecurityIssuesPrefix: For security-relevant accessibility issues, please use our
accessibilityPage.grievanceIntro: {{libraryName}} provides equal access to its services, programs, and activities. If you believe you were denied access to, or discriminated against in, a library service, program, or activity on the basis of disability, you may file a grievance under Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).
accessibilityPage.hearing1: Hearing loop system at service desks
accessibilityPage.hearing4: ASL interpretation upon request for events
accessibilityPage.howToFilePrefix: Submit your grievance in writing, or in another accessible format on request, to the ADA Coordinator at
accessibilityPage.howToFileSuffix: . Please include your name, how to reach you, a description of what happened, the date it occurred, and the resolution you are seeking.
accessibilityPage.howWeWork1: Every public-facing page has an automated accessibility test in our test suite.
accessibilityPage.howWeWork2: Calm-mode, focus-mode, high-contrast theme, and customizable text density ship as core features, not add-ons.
accessibilityPage.howWeWork3: We treat keyboard navigation as a primary input, not a fallback.
accessibilityPage.howWeWork4: Patron-facing accessibility services are listed below; the rest of this page is for end-user accommodations.
accessibilityPage.knownGap1: Some legacy admin views ship without complete keyboard-only flows — replacements in progress.
accessibilityPage.knownGap2: Color contrast in a few branded-theme combinations needs re-checking after recent BrandingContext changes.
accessibilityPage.knownGap3: Alt-text coverage on user-uploaded images depends on staff entry; admin tooling for review is being added.
accessibilityPage.noRetaliationText: The library will not retaliate against anyone for filing a grievance or for participating in the resolution of one.
accessibilityPage.physical5: Home delivery service for patrons who cannot visit
accessibilityPage.recordRetentionValue: Grievances and the library's responses are retained for 3 years.
accessibilityPage.responseValue: The ADA Coordinator will respond in writing within 15 business days, in a format accessible to you, and will work with you to resolve the issue.
accessibilityPage.targetStandardValue: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, Level AA
accessibilityPage.visual2: Screen magnification software on public computers
accessibilityPage.visual3: JAWS and NVDA screen readers available
accessibilityPage.visual5: Braille materials and BARD access (BARD is a free audiobook library from the Library of Congress for people with reading disabilities)
accessibilityPage.wcagComplianceIntro: We strive to comply with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA and applicable accessibility standards. We are continuously working to improve the accessibility of our website and services.
accessibilityPage.whenToFileValue: As soon as possible, and ideally within 60 calendar days of the alleged barrier or discrimination.

privacyPage.alaGuidelinesIntro: We follow the American Library Association's guidelines on patron confidentiality. Your reading records and library usage are private.
privacyPage.analyticsAggregateOnly: We only see aggregate information like which pages are most visited and what devices people use
privacyPage.analyticsNoCookies: No cookies are set by our analytics
privacyPage.analyticsSelfHosted: All data is self-hosted on our own servers — never shared with third parties
privacyPage.analyticsUmamiIntro: We use Umami, a privacy-respecting analytics tool, to understand how people use our website. This helps us improve our services.
privacyPage.changesNoticeText: Changes to this sub-processor list are communicated at least 30 days in advance to operating institutions via email and a dated changelog at this URL.
privacyPage.chatAssistantIntro: When you use the library’s chat assistant (for example, “Ask a Librarian”), here’s what happens to what you type:
privacyPage.chatKeepConversation: We keep the conversation so a staff member can follow up if you ask, and so we can fix problems. If you leave an email for follow-up, it is stored with that conversation and used only to reply to you.
privacyPage.chatNeverTrainStrong: never used to train an AI model
privacyPage.chatOwnServersSuffix: . They are not sent to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or any outside AI company.
privacyPage.chatRetentionText: Chat assistant conversations are deleted within 90 days. For staff-only AI tools, the text you type is removed after 30 days and the log is deleted within 90.
privacyPage.chatStaysOnServersPrefix: What you type and the assistant's replies stay on the library's
privacyPage.cloudflareDataScope: IP addresses, HTTP request headers, TLS termination
privacyPage.collectBorrowingHistory: Borrowing history (you control this — opt in to keep your reading history, or leave it off and records are cleared after items are returned)
privacyPage.collectRegistration: Name, address, and contact information for library card registration
privacyPage.collectUsageStats: Computer and Wi-Fi usage statistics (anonymized means we track how often and when people use these services, but we do not track who uses them or what websites are visited)
privacyPage.committedToProtecting: {{libraryName}} is committed to protecting your privacy and ensuring the confidentiality of your personal information.
privacyPage.conditionalMeansSuffix: means the sub-processor is used only when the corresponding feature is enabled in your deployment. Self-hosted customers control which are active.
privacyPage.confidentialityCoverage: This protection covers your borrowing history, holds, search and browsing activity, computer and Wi-Fi use, program registrations, and any personally identifying information in your library account.
privacyPage.cookieAuthSuffix: — keeps you logged in between visits. This is a secure, encrypted cookie that cannot be read by other websites. It is deleted when you log out.
privacyPage.cookieLocalPrefsSuffix: — your accessibility settings, theme choice, and reading preferences are stored in your browser (not on our servers) and never shared.
privacyPage.cookiesEssentialOnly: We use only essential cookies required for the site to function. We do not use advertising, tracking, or third-party cookies.
privacyPage.coppaConsent: A parent or guardian must provide consent before a child under 13 can create an account
privacyPage.coppaMinimumInfo: We collect only the minimum information needed to provide library services to children
privacyPage.coppaNoSharing: Children's browsing and reading history is never shared or used for recommendations without parental consent
privacyPage.coppaParentsReview: Parents can review, update, or request deletion of their child's information at any time
privacyPage.dataResidencyText: Primary patron data is stored on self-hosted infrastructure. Cloudflare edge nodes terminate TLS globally; no patron-identifying data is cached at edge. US-based sub-processors handle data under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or Standard Contractual Clauses where applicable.
privacyPage.disclosureLegalProcess: In response to a valid court order, subpoena, or other legal process, as required by law
privacyPage.disclosureOtherwisePermitted: As otherwise required or permitted by Ohio Revised Code § 149.432
privacyPage.disclosureToStaff: To library staff acting within the scope of their duties to operate the library
privacyPage.disclosureToYou: To you, or to a person you authorize in writing
privacyPage.ferpaBorrowingHistoryPrefix: Borrowing history, reading recommendations, and search queries are
privacyPage.ferpaDataSharingAgreementPrefix: A FERPA-compliant Data Sharing Agreement is available for K-12 and higher-ed customers on request — email
privacyPage.ferpaIntro: When Librar is deployed at a K-12 school, district, or higher-education institution, patron records may be considered "education records" under the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA, 20 U.S.C. § 1232g). In that context:
privacyPage.ferpaNeitherOursSuffix: — neither ours nor any third party's.
privacyPage.ferpaNoAdvertising: We do not use student data for advertising, marketing to students, or any purpose other than delivering library services.
privacyPage.ferpaNotUsedToTrainStrong: not used to train AI models
privacyPage.ferpaSchoolOfficialStrong: school official with a legitimate educational interest
privacyPage.ferpaStudentRecordsReleased: Student records are released only to the institution, to the student or parent exercising FERPA rights, or under valid legal process (subpoena, court order, judicial warrant).
privacyPage.ferpaWhenProcessingSuffix: when processing student records on behalf of the operating institution.
privacyPage.githubPurpose: Build-time container image storage (no patron data ever)
privacyPage.leNoVoluntarySharing: We do not voluntarily share patron records with law enforcement or government agencies
privacyPage.leNotifyPatrons: We will notify affected patrons of requests for their records unless legally prohibited from doing so
privacyPage.leRequestsReviewed: All law enforcement requests are reviewed by library administration and logged
privacyPage.leRequireCourtOrder: We require a valid court order, subpoena, or warrant before releasing any patron information
privacyPage.noConsentBannerNeeded: No consent banner is needed because we only use strictly necessary cookies.
privacyPage.ohioLawIntro: Ohio law protects the privacy of library users. Under Ohio Revised Code § 149.432, any library record that identifies you as having requested, used, or borrowed library materials or services is confidential. We will not disclose it except:
privacyPage.openaiDataScope: Catalog item titles, descriptions, subject headings
privacyPage.openaiPurpose: Embeddings API for catalog semantic search — catalog text only, never patron data
privacyPage.privateEmailPurpose: Staff inbox hosting (info@, security@, privacy@, accessibility@)
privacyPage.protectionEncryption: Encrypted data transmission and storage (your information is scrambled when sent to our servers and locked in secure storage, so others cannot read it)
privacyPage.protectionLimitedAccess: Limited access to personal information (only a small number of authorized staff members can view your personal details, and only when needed to help you)
privacyPage.protectionStaffTraining: Staff training on privacy and confidentiality
privacyPage.questionsIntro: If you have questions about this privacy policy or how we handle your information, please contact us:
privacyPage.recordsConfidentialityHeading: Confidentiality of Library Records (Ohio Revised Code § 149.432)
privacyPage.resendDataScope: Recipient email address, notification message body
privacyPage.resendPurpose: Transactional email delivery (holds, due-date notices, account notifications)
privacyPage.retentionText: Borrowing history retention is patron-controlled (opt-in). Request/IP metadata is retained for 30 days for security investigation, then purged. Backup snapshots roll off within 90 days. On account deletion, personally-identifying records are removed from the primary database within 7 days; remaining backup snapshots roll off within the standard backup window.
privacyPage.rightAccessInfo: Access your personal information upon request
privacyPage.sentryDataScope: Stack traces, request paths; no patron PII in scrubbed payload
privacyPage.stripePurpose: Payment processing — card data handled by Stripe via PCI-compliant iframe; L30 never sees card numbers
privacyPage.subProcessorsIntroPrefix: To deliver Librar's services, we use a small set of trusted sub-processors. Each is listed below with its purpose, the data in scope, and where it operates. A Data Processing Addendum (DPA) is available on request — email
privacyPage.useImproveServices: To improve our services and programs
privacyPage.useProvideServices: To provide library services and manage your account
privacyPage.useSendNotifications: To send notifications about holds, due dates, and events
privacyPage.weBelieveThatPrivacy: We believe that privacy is a fundamental right. This policy explains how we collect, use, and protect your personal information when you use our library services, website, and digital resources.
privacyPage.weTakeExtraCare: We take extra care with information about children under 13, in accordance with the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA).

termsPage.agreementText1: These Terms of Service govern your use of the {{libraryName}}'s website, digital resources, and all related services. wifiPage.pageDescription: Connect to free high-speed WiFi at {{libraryShortName}}. Network name, password, and connection instructions.
wifiPage.heading: Free High-Speed WiFi
wifiPage.intro: Connect to our library network and enjoy high-speed internet access from anywhere in the building.
wifiPage.desktopStep1: 1. Click the WiFi icon in your system tray/menu bar
wifiPage.desktopStep4: 4. Open your browser - you may see a login page (optional)
wifiPage.a1: Try turning WiFi off and back on, or restart your device. If the network still doesn't appear, ask a staff member at the front desk - we may be experiencing a technical issue.
wifiPage.a2: Double-check the password is entered exactly as shown above. Passwords are case-sensitive. If you're still having trouble, visit the front desk or tech support area.
wifiPage.a3: Try "forgetting" the network and reconnecting. Or restart your device. If the problem persists, speak with our tech support staff - they can help diagnose the issue.
wifiPage.a4: WiFi speed depends on how many people are connected. Try moving closer to a router or ask staff where the strongest signal is located. For demanding tasks, our public computers offer a wired connection.
wifiPage.stillTroubleBody: Our tech support team is here to help! Visit the tech support desk or ask any staff member for assistance.

securityPage.heading: Security & Responsible Disclosure
securityPage.subheading: How to report a vulnerability in L30
securityPage.privacyCalloutPre: Looking for how we protect your personal information and keep your reading history private? That is on our
securityPage.privacyCalloutPost: This page is for reporting a security vulnerability.
securityPage.foundIssueHeading: If you found a security issue
securityPage.foundIssueBody: We welcome reports from security researchers, library staff, patrons, and anyone else who finds a vulnerability in L30 or any service we operate. Email a description and reproduction steps to:
securityPage.pgpNote: For sensitive disclosures, request our PGP key in your first email and we will reply with it.
securityPage.expectSafeHarborRest: We will not pursue legal action against researchers acting in good faith under this policy.
securityPage.expectCoordinatedRest: Please give us reasonable time (typically 90 days) before public disclosure.
securityPage.expectCreditRest: If you’d like attribution after the fix ships, we’ll list you in our acknowledgements.
securityPage.inScope1: l30.org and any subdomain we operate
securityPage.inScope3: Data exposure (patron records, staff records, catalog data)
securityPage.inScope5: Workflow bypass affecting circulation, holds, or fines
securityPage.outOfScope2: Spam, phishing, or social engineering of staff
securityPage.outOfScope3: Issues in third-party services we use (please report directly to them)
securityPage.outOfScope5: Outdated software with no proven exploit
securityPage.outOfScope6: Physical attacks or attacks requiring local access
securityPage.dont1: Access, modify, or destroy data that isn’t yours.
securityPage.dont3: Publicly disclose the issue before we’ve had a chance to fix it.
securityPage.dont4: Use automated scanners that generate substantial traffic.
